questions.questionText:
Attendance in the first lecture of the day has dropped sharply in a first-year class, though attendance in later lectures is normal.

Courses of Action:
I. Survey the students to find out whether transport, timetable or health issues are responsible, and adjust accordingly.
II. Provide a recording of the first lecture so that a student who misses it can catch up before the next class.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I addresses the actual reason for the drop and can be implemented immediately. Course II is appropriate because it limits the loss caused by a missed lecture and costs very little to arrange. Therefore, both courses I and II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A department has only enough laboratory equipment for half of each practical batch, so students spend most of the session waiting.

Courses of Action:
I. Split each batch into two groups that rotate through the practical on separate days.
II. Schedule practical batches in the afternoon as well so that the equipment is used through the day.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both courses should be implemented.
Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I uses the available equipment efficiently and keeps practical learning going. Course II is appropriate because the same equipment then serves more students each week. Therefore, both courses should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
A large number of second-year students have failed in a core subject that is a prerequisite for the next semester.

Courses of Action:
I. Conduct remedial classes and weekly practice tests for the failed students before the next semester begins.
II. Counsel the failed students individually so that each one can plan how to clear the subject in the supplementary examination.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I gives the struggling students the support needed to clear a prerequisite subject. Course II is appropriate because it addresses the individual reasons for failure and gives each student a plan for the next attempt. Therefore, both courses are justified.

questions.questionText:
Invigilators have reported that some students copied answers during the last university examination.

Courses of Action:
I. Announce on the notice board that strict action will be taken against copying, without changing the examination arrangements.
II. Cancel the results of the entire batch for that examination.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I is inappropriate because a general warning leaves the invigilation and seating weaknesses that made the copying possible entirely unchanged. Course II punishes students who did nothing wrong and is disproportionate to the reported incident. Therefore, neither is a reasonable course of action.

questions.questionText:
The syllabus of a computer science programme has not been revised for eight years and students report that it does not reflect current industry practice.

Courses of Action:
I. Ask the students to learn the current industry tools on their own outside the syllabus.
II. Drop the fundamental subjects and replace them with the latest tools.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I leaves the responsibility for the syllabus with the students themselves and does not change what the college teaches. Course II sacrifices the foundations on which advanced subjects depend and would harm students' long-term learning. Therefore, neither course should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Several students in a college are unable to pay their fees on time because of sudden family financial difficulties, and they face being barred from examinations.

Courses of Action:
I. Set up a fee-instalment and scholarship-guidance desk that evaluates each case against college norms.
II. Write off the entire fee dues of every student who claims financial difficulty.
III. Ask the college's alumni association to fund the fees of every student who applies for help.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Courses I and II should be followed.
All three courses should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I gives genuine cases a practical route while keeping the process verifiable. Course II is financially unworkable for the college and gives no verification of the claims. Course III is inappropriate because it commits alumni funds without any assessment of need, and the association has no obligation or capacity to meet every request. Therefore, only course I should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A department has been running with four vacancies for two months and the remaining faculty members are overloaded.

Courses of Action:
I. Appoint visiting faculty for the current semester while a regular recruitment process continues.
II. Reallocate the teaching load so that the core subjects of the vacant posts are covered first until recruitment is completed.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.
Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I restores teaching capacity quickly without disturbing the recruitment process. Course II is appropriate because it protects the learning of the most important subjects while the posts remain vacant. Therefore, both courses should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
Students have complained of severe stress because several departments schedule assignment deadlines and internal tests in the same week.

Courses of Action:
I. Review the academic calendar centrally and stagger deadlines and internal tests across departments.
II. Cancel all assignments and internal tests for the semester.
III. Allow a short grace window for students who have three or more submissions due in the same week.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: None of the courses should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course III should be followed.
Courses I and III should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I removes the cause of the stress while preserving continuous assessment. Course II removes an essential part of evaluation and would reduce student effort rather than manage workload. Course III is appropriate because it gives relief to the small group that is genuinely over-committed while the calendar is being corrected. Therefore, courses I and III should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A newly introduced elective requires six reference books, but the college library has only one copy of each and demand is high.

Courses of Action:
I. Subscribe to the e-book versions, place adequate copies in the reference section and set short loan periods.
II. Keep a copy of the essential chapters in the department reading room for consultation by the students of the elective.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I increases genuine availability of the material. Course II is appropriate because it makes the required content available at once from material the department already holds. Therefore, both courses are justified.

questions.questionText:
A handful of students regularly arrive twenty minutes late for the first lecture, disturbing the class.

Courses of Action:
I. Shorten the first lecture by twenty minutes for the whole class so that latecomers disturb it less.
II. Refuse entry to the classroom to every student who arrives after the first minute.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I reduces the teaching time of every student in order to accommodate the few who arrive late. Course II penalises the whole class for the habit of a few and may cause students to skip the lecture entirely. Therefore, neither is a reasonable course of action.

questions.questionText:
There have been two minor accidents in the chemistry laboratory this semester because students were unfamiliar with safety procedures.

Courses of Action:
I. Paste a notice in the laboratory listing the safety rules and ask the students to read it.
II. Close the student laboratory permanently to eliminate the risk.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I assumes that reading a notice will change behaviour and leaves the practical safety training that prevents accidents untouched. Course II removes practical education from the programme, which is a disproportionate and educationally damaging response. Therefore, neither course should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Results of end-semester examinations are published two months late every year, delaying internships and higher-study applications.

Courses of Action:
I. Automate the evaluation workflow and commit to a published result date with an escalation mechanism.
II. Publish incomplete results as soon as they are available rather than waiting for verification.
III. Declare the results of only the subjects that are ready and leave the remaining subjects indefinitely.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I should be followed.
Only course III should be followed.
Courses I and III should be followed.
None of the courses should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I fixes the delay through process improvement while keeping results reliable. Course II shifts the burden of an internal problem onto students by releasing unverified marks. Course III institutionalises the delay and leaves students with an incomplete result at a time when they need it for applications. Therefore, only course I should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Many first-year students who come from regional-language schools struggle with mathematics and fall behind in engineering subjects.

Courses of Action:
I. Run a bridge course in the first weeks and pair weaker students with trained peer mentors.
II. Ask the subject teachers to identify students who are falling behind within the first month and give them targeted help.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I builds the missing foundation and keeps students on track for the full programme. Course II is appropriate because early identification reaches the students who need support before the gap becomes large. Therefore, both courses should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
Students in a hostel have complained repeatedly about the quality and hygiene of the mess food.

Courses of Action:
I. Form a student-faculty mess committee that audits hygiene, inspects supplies and revises the menu periodically.
II. Publish the weekly mess menu and collect student feedback on each meal.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I creates accountable monitoring of the mess and can improve it. Course II is appropriate because it gives the residents a voice in what is served and makes the quality visible to the committee. Therefore, both courses are justified.

questions.questionText:
Wi-Fi connectivity in the campus drops frequently, especially in the second-floor classrooms and the library reading hall.

Courses of Action:
I. Audit network coverage, upgrade access points in the affected zones and monitor link quality.
II. Withdraw internet access from hostels and common areas to reduce load.
III. Reimburse the students' mobile data charges for a semester instead of restoring the network.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: None of the courses should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Courses II and III should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I addresses the technical cause of the outages and restores service where it is needed. Course II degrades services that are not the problem and worsens student experience. Course III pays to bypass the problem instead of restoring connectivity, and it would not help in the laboratories and classrooms where the network is genuinely required. Therefore, only course I should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Final-year students complain that their project guides are rarely available for consultation and projects are slipping.

Courses of Action:
I. Publish a fixed weekly consultation schedule for every guide with a named alternative for slots that are missed.
II. Assign a co-guide to each project group so that guidance continues when the main guide is unavailable.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I makes guidance reliable and keeps the project on schedule. Course II is appropriate because it removes the dependence of a project group on one person's availability. Therefore, both are reasonable courses of action.

questions.questionText:
The biometric attendance system records students as absent even when they attend classes, and the faults recur.

Courses of Action:
I. Get the devices serviced, calibrate them and run a manual fallback register whenever the system fails.
II. Record the attendance manually on the days the system fails and merge the register with the device data.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I restores accurate records and keeps a working fallback during failures. Course II is appropriate because it keeps the attendance records correct during the recurring failures. Therefore, both courses I and II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Many students were unaware of the minimum academic criteria for campus placement eligibility and were turned away at the registration desk.

Courses of Action:
I. Publish the eligibility criteria on the placement portal and brief students well before the recruitment season starts.
II. Run a short training programme for students who fall short of specific criteria so that they can meet them in time.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both courses should be implemented.
Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I gives students timely information so that they can prepare. Course II is appropriate because it helps students reach the eligibility standard instead of only informing them about it. Therefore, both courses should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
A group of students has disputed the marks awarded in a practical viva, claiming that the evaluation was inconsistent.

Courses of Action:
I. Increase the marks of every student in the practical viva by ten per cent so that no one feels treated unfairly.
II. Award full marks to every student who raised the dispute.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I changes the marks of a whole batch without examining any of them and destroys the meaning of the assessment. Course II rewards the complaint rather than addressing the inconsistency and would be unfair to other students. Therefore, neither course is justified.

questions.questionText:
Students have requested access to their evaluated answer scripts for the internal assessments, which the college does not allow.

Courses of Action:
I. Allow a structured review window in which scripts are shown and genuine correction requests are processed.
II. Refuse all disclosure in order to protect the faculty members from questions.
III. Photograph the evaluated scripts and show the images to students who request a review within a week.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: None of the courses should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course III should be followed.
Courses I and III should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I satisfies a legitimate request while keeping the process orderly. Course II treats a reasonable transparency measure as a threat and leaves genuine errors uncorrected. Course III is appropriate because it makes the review quick and can be operated with the staff who are already available. Therefore, courses I and III should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A large proportion of students who have moved from other states are finding it difficult to follow lectures conducted in the local language.

Courses of Action:
I. Provide bilingual handouts, key-term glossaries and recorded summaries for the affected subjects.
II. Arrange a peer buddy for each affected student so that the lecture content can be explained in a familiar language.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I is a practical support measure that can be arranged immediately. Course II is appropriate because it gives those students immediate help in following the lectures. Therefore, both are reasonable courses of action.

questions.questionText:
The college playground is uneven and unmarked, and students have stopped using it for practice.

Courses of Action:
I. Prepare a maintenance plan, level the ground, mark the courts and assign periodic upkeep duties.
II. Appoint a caretaker for the ground and include its upkeep in the annual maintenance budget.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I restores the facility through scheduled maintenance. Course II is appropriate because it keeps the facility in usable condition after the levelling work is done. Therefore, both courses I and II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Fewer than twenty students have joined any of the technical clubs this year.

Courses of Action:
I. Hold an activity fair, invite club members to demonstrate projects, and support student-led events with small budgets.
II. Make membership in a technical club compulsory with penalties for non-participation.
III. Award academic credit for sustained and verified participation in a technical club.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course II should be followed.
Courses I and III should be followed.
All three courses should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I increases interest by showing students what the clubs offer. Course II forces participation, which produces attendance without engagement. Course III is appropriate because it gives students a concrete reason to participate and recognises the effort they put into club work. Therefore, courses I and III should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Elective examinations for two different subjects have been scheduled in the same slot, and about sixty students are enrolled in both.

Courses of Action:
I. Ask the examiners to conduct both papers one after the other in a single extended session.
II. Ask the affected students to prepare for both papers in the same slot.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I expects candidates to write two papers in one sitting, which the examination schedule does not permit and which would harm every candidate's performance. Course II is simply impossible for the students to comply with. Therefore, neither course should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
Students of a new elective cannot buy the prescribed textbook because the publisher's stock is not available locally.

Courses of Action:
I. Change the syllabus of the elective midway through the semester.
II. Arrange a central bulk purchase and keep multiple library reference copies for the semester.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course II solves the shortage practically and keeps the course stable. Course I disrupts teaching mid-semester to avoid an administrative inconvenience. Therefore, only course II is justified.

questions.questionText:
Faculty members report that students spend much of the lecture using mobile phones, and classroom attention is poor.

Courses of Action:
I. Announce a clear device policy with a collection point at the entrance and include short in-class activities that require attention.
II. Explain the device policy to the students and publish the consequences clearly before it is enforced.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I sets an enforceable expectation and improves engagement. Course II is appropriate because a rule of this kind is followed only when students understand it and know the consequences in advance. Therefore, both are reasonable courses of action.

questions.questionText:
There is no formal channel for students to comment on course delivery, and grievances surface only as complaints at the end of the year.

Courses of Action:
I. Introduce anonymous mid-course feedback with a published summary of the actions taken on it.
II. Ask students to message individual lecturers on their personal phone numbers.
III. Collect the feedback and forward it to the head of the institution without telling the students what changes.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I should be followed.
Courses I and II should be followed.
Courses II and III should be followed.
All three courses should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I creates a structured and anonymous channel that leads to action. Course II is disorderly, gives no anonymity and provides no mechanism for follow-up. Course III repeats the existing weakness, since comments are collected but nothing that follows is communicated back to the students. Therefore, only course I should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Students who have completed their degrees wait weeks for their certificates because records are verified manually.

Courses of Action:
I. Digitise the academic records and commit to a published service timeline for certificate issue.
II. Give every applicant a case reference and an expected delivery date that can be checked online.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I removes the underlying cause of the delay. Course II is appropriate because it makes the revised process accountable and tells applicants where their certificate stands. Therefore, both courses I and II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
The number of research papers published by the faculty of a college has fallen over the last three years.

Courses of Action:
I. Provide seed grants, protect research time and recognise publications in faculty appraisal.
II. Adjust the teaching load of the faculty who take up research so that they have time for it.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.
Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I creates realistic incentives and support for faculty research. Course II is appropriate because research needs protected time, and the adjustment can be planned within the existing staff strength. Therefore, both courses should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
Laboratory assistants have not received any technical training since the equipment in the central laboratory was upgraded.

Courses of Action:
I. Arrange structured technical training and certification for the assistants before the next academic year.
II. Ask the equipment supplier to train the laboratory assistants during the annual maintenance visit.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I closes the skills gap that causes operating problems. Course II is appropriate because the supplier can provide the training as part of the equipment support at little extra cost. Therefore, both courses are justified.

questions.questionText:
Students living far from the campus find it difficult to attend the eight o'clock lectures and their attendance has fallen sharply.

Courses of Action:
I. Suspend all morning lectures for the whole college.
II. Make recordings and study material available and shift the lectures that can be rescheduled to later slots.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I abandons the academic timetable for everyone, though only a section of students is affected. Course II combines a practical support measure with a feasible timetable adjustment and addresses the difficulty directly. Therefore, course II is the better course of action.

questions.questionText:
The central library is overcrowded during examination weeks and students wait for seats.

Courses of Action:
I. Restrict the library to final-year students during examination weeks.
II. Extend library hours and open two temporary reading halls during the examination period.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I denies access to students who are equally entitled to the facility. Course II expands capacity in proportion to the peak demand and can be implemented for a short period. Therefore, only course II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Laboratory reports of the first-year batch are submitted late by most students and records pile up at the end of the semester.

Courses of Action:
I. Reject every late report without exception, whatever the reason.
II. Publish submission dates at the start of the semester and allow a short, uniformly applied grace period.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both courses should be implemented.
Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I is inflexible and creates grievances without preventing the delay. Course II removes the cause of late submission by informing students in advance and keeps a fair, uniform rule. Therefore, course II should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
The information-security module taught in the final year still covers practices that are several years out of date.

Courses of Action:
I. Remove the module from the programme.
II. Re-design the module with practitioners and update case studies and tools each year.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I leaves students without knowledge that employers expect. Course II updates content in a sustainable way and directly addresses the obsolete syllabus. Therefore, only course II is justified.

questions.questionText:
Placement training sessions have been clashing with laboratory sessions, so students are missing both.

Courses of Action:
I. Cancel placement training for the semester.
II. Reschedule the training and laboratory sessions on a common timetable after consulting both departments.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I removes training that students need for recruitment. Course II removes the clash itself by coordinating two departments, which is the real source of the problem. Therefore, course II is the better course of action.

questions.questionText:
The library loses several books every semester and the checkout counter relies on manual registers.

Courses of Action:
I. Take a large refundable deposit from every student at the start of the year.
II. Introduce electronic checkout, security tagging at the exit and periodic stock verification.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I penalises all students for the losses of a few and discourages genuine readers. Course II targets the weakness in the lending system that causes the losses. Therefore, only course II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Students in the larger lecture halls complain that they cannot hear the lecturer clearly.

Courses of Action:
I. Ask students to occupy only the front rows.
II. Install and maintain a public-address system in the large halls and check it before each semester.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I is a limited instruction that does not solve the problem for most students. Course II addresses the acoustic limitation of the halls and benefits everyone in the class. Therefore, course II should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
Internship certificates submitted by a batch of students are pending verification, and the placement office has not processed them for weeks.

Courses of Action:
I. Ask the students to obtain the verification themselves from the companies.
II. Create a standard verification process with fixed timelines and a responsible officer in the placement cell.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I transfers an administrative task to students and does not fix the delay. Course II corrects the internal process that caused the delay. Therefore, only course II is justified.

questions.questionText:
A set of internal question papers was found to contain ambiguous questions and errors in a language section.

Courses of Action:
I. Reuse the same question bank for the next cycle to save effort.
II. Set up a review committee with a question blueprint and a proof-reading stage before papers are finalised.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I guarantees that the same errors recur. Course II introduces quality checks at the point where the defects are created. Therefore, course II is the better course of action.

questions.questionText:
Tutorial sessions are poorly attended and students who need help are not using them.

Courses of Action:
I. Issue a warning notice to every tutorial group in the college.
II. Discuss with students why the sessions are unattractive, restructure them and track attendance by group.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I is a vague, blanket warning that does not change anything. Course II diagnoses the reason for poor attendance and adapts the sessions to the students' needs. Therefore, only course II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Students walking between the library and the hostel after 8 p.m. have complained of poor lighting and a lack of security.

Courses of Action:
I. Improve lighting and patrolling on the affected routes.
II. Introduce an on-call escort and a safety-awareness campaign for students.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I removes the immediate safety risk on the routes. Course II adds a support mechanism and awareness so that students can move safely. The two are complementary and both should be followed. Therefore, both courses should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
Hostel residents face water shortages in the early morning because of leakages and rising demand.

Courses of Action:
I. Repair leaking pipelines and audit daily water usage in the hostels.
II. Install additional storage tanks and rainwater-harvesting arrangements on the hostel blocks.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I reduces the loss and waste that cause the shortage. Course II increases the supply capacity for the long term. Both are feasible and address different aspects of the same problem. Therefore, both courses are justified.

questions.questionText:
The first-year dropout rate has doubled, and most of those who leave were academically weak from the first month.

Courses of Action:
I. Introduce a mentor scheme in which every teacher supports a small group of students.
II. Set up a doubt-clearing and academic-support centre that opens before the first internal test.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I provides early personal support and identifies students at risk. Course II gives additional academic help at the stage when weakness begins. Both strengthen the same early-warning effort. Therefore, both are reasonable courses of action.

questions.questionText:
Campus restrooms in two blocks are reported to be unclean almost every week.

Courses of Action:
I. Fix a supervised cleaning schedule with signed checklists for each block.
II. Provide a complaint tracker through which staff and students can report problems for same-day action.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I creates routine accountability for cleanliness. Course II provides a fast route for exceptional problems. Both are practical and together they sustain hygiene. Therefore, both courses I and II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A fire audit has pointed out that the hostel has no working alarms and that students do not know the evacuation route.

Courses of Action:
I. Conduct a fire-safety audit follow-up, repair the alarm system and install extinguishers on every floor.
II. Hold a mandatory evacuation drill every semester and display the exit maps in every corridor.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both courses should be implemented.
Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I removes the physical hazard identified in the audit. Course II prepares the students to respond if a fire does occur. Both should be followed because prevention and preparedness are needed together. Therefore, both courses should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
About ninety students have fallen below the minimum attendance requirement and will be detained unless their cases are reviewed.

Courses of Action:
I. Constitute a review committee that examines genuine cases such as illness on the basis of documents.
II. Introduce an early-warning system that alerts students and parents when attendance falls below eighty-five per cent.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I fairly resolves the cases that have already arisen. Course II reduces the number of such cases in future. Both are reasonable and address the present and the future aspects of the issue. Therefore, both courses are justified.

questions.questionText:
The admission counter takes more than two hours per candidate during the peak week and applicants wait in long queues.

Courses of Action:
I. Move the application and document verification process to an online portal with a document checklist.
II. Deploy additional staff at the counters and open a second verification hall during the peak week.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I reduces the workload by redesigning the process. Course II adds immediate capacity where the crowd is highest. Both are practical and address the same delay from different directions. Therefore, both are reasonable courses of action.

questions.questionText:
A survey shows that most students have never used the library's online journal subscriptions.

Courses of Action:
I. Run short orientation sessions on how to search the subscribed databases.
II. Circulate a subject-wise guide to the available journals and databases through the departments.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I teaches students to use resources that are already paid for. Course II makes the same resources visible at the point of need. Both are inexpensive and directly relevant. Therefore, both courses I and II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Reports of copying in the previous internal examination have disrupted confidence in the assessment process.

Courses of Action:
I. Brief the invigilation team on procedures and rotate invigilators randomly across halls.
II. Announce a clear zero-tolerance policy with a fair, documented enquiry process for suspected cases.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.
Neither course should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I strengthens the conduct of the examination itself. Course II provides a transparent deterrent and a fair procedure. Both are necessary to protect the credibility of the assessment. Therefore, both courses should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
Participation in the annual technical festival has fallen, and most events are attended only by students of the host college.

Courses of Action:
I. Invite nearby colleges, publish the events online and open registration to all.
II. Plan department-wise technical events so that every student has at least one event to enter.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I widens the audience and raises the scale of the festival. Course II increases participation from within the college. Both are relevant, practical and mutually supporting. Therefore, both courses are justified.

questions.questionText:
A few students have failed the same subject in three consecutive attempts and the department is under pressure to act.

Courses of Action:
I. Remove the subject from the programme's requirement list.
II. Promote all students of that subject regardless of their performance.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I weakens the programme and the value of the degree. Course II destroys the credibility of assessment and is unfair to students who passed on merit. Neither course of action addresses the students' actual difficulty. Therefore, neither is a reasonable course of action.

questions.questionText:
During the annual festival week, complaints about littering and unclean common areas have increased sharply.

Courses of Action:
I. Ban all student events on the campus with immediate effect.
II. Ask the teaching staff to carry out the cleaning work themselves during the festival.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I is a disproportionate response that cancels student activities altogether. Course II is an impractical duty that does not match the staff's role or numbers. Neither course addresses the behaviour that causes the littering. Therefore, neither course should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A critical application server reaches full CPU usage every day around 11 a.m. and users face slow responses for about twenty minutes.

Courses of Action:
I. Restart the server automatically every morning at eleven o'clock.
II. Study the usage logs and load pattern of that period and tune the application or shift part of the load.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course II identifies and fixes the cause of the peak load. Course I only masks the symptom for a short while and interrupts service while it treats the problem as routine maintenance. Therefore, course II should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
A nightly data-synchronisation job fails two or three times a week and nobody notices until users complain.

Courses of Action:
I. Add monitoring and alerting for the job and analyse the failure logs to correct the underlying error.
II. Disable the job so that no failures are reported.
III. Run the synchronisation job manually every night so that someone is watching it.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: None of the courses should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course III should be followed.
Courses I and III should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I detects failures early and corrects the error that causes them. Course II stops the data synchronisation itself, which would create fresh data inconsistencies. Course III substitutes manual supervision for a repair, which depends on a person being available every night and leaves the fault in place. Therefore, only course I should be followed.

questions.questionText:
The effect of a recent software release is that the login page of an internal application returns errors for some users.

Courses of Action:
I. Ask the affected users to try a different browser and continue working until the matter is investigated.
II. Ask the affected users to wait until the next scheduled release in three months.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I assumes the fault lies with the users' software, which nothing in the report supports, and it leaves them without a solution. Course II leaves users without access for months, which is disproportionate to a fixable defect. Therefore, neither course is justified.

questions.questionText:
Several employees have reported suspicious emails asking them to re-enter their office passwords on a linked page.

Courses of Action:
I. Change the organisation's internet service provider to reduce the number of phishing messages.
II. Disable external email for the whole organisation until the matter is forgotten.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I addresses the delivery route rather than the messages themselves and would not reduce the attempts being made. Course II cuts off a business-critical channel and is far too extreme for a phishing wave. Therefore, neither is a reasonable course of action.

questions.questionText:
Malware has been detected on one office laptop that is connected to the corporate network.

Courses of Action:
I. Reinstall the operating system on the laptop on the next convenient day and continue working until then.
II. Ignore the detection because only one machine is affected.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I leaves an infected machine connected until a convenient day, which provides none of the containment the situation calls for. Course II assumes that a single detection is harmless, which is not justified by the information given. Therefore, neither course should be followed.

questions.questionText:
An audit found that many employees use short passwords that are common English words and reuse them across systems.

Courses of Action:
I. Enforce a password policy with multi-factor authentication and provide a password manager.
II. Circulate a list of the weakest passwords currently in use so that staff can change them.
III. Circulate the list of accounts that failed the password audit so that colleagues can be careful with them.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: None of the courses should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Courses II and III should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I raises the standard of authentication across the organisation. Course II exposes weak credentials more widely and increases the risk rather than reducing it. Course III is inappropriate because it identifies the weakest accounts to the whole organisation and would expose exactly the accounts that are most at risk. Therefore, only course I should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A former employee's account was still active a month after the person left the company.

Courses of Action:
I. Change the display name on the account so that it is clear that the user has left.
II. Leave the account in place so that former employees can be contacted if required.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.
Neither course should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I only relabels the account and leaves its credentials fully usable. Course II keeps an unnecessary and risky access route open. Therefore, neither course should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
A public web server is running an older version of its software for which a security patch has been available for weeks.

Courses of Action:
I. Test and apply the patch in the next maintenance window and verify the service afterwards.
II. Track security advisories for all publicly accessible software and apply updates within a defined period.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I removes the vulnerability in a controlled way. Course II is appropriate because it creates a continuing process so that the same vulnerability does not remain unpatched again. Therefore, both courses are justified.

questions.questionText:
The same disk in a storage array has failed twice in six months and the array is out of warranty.

Courses of Action:
I. Replace the failed disk, analyse the health of the array, and plan a phased refresh of the ageing hardware.
II. Continue using the array and address the disk only when the storage stops working.
III. Move the array's data to a cloud service immediately without planning the cost or the connectivity.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Courses I and III should be followed.
All three courses should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I deals with the present failure and reduces the chance of a larger outage. Course II waits for a failure that would interrupt services. Course III is a large change taken without planning cost, connectivity or recovery, and the information given does not justify it at this stage. Therefore, only course I should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Employees report that the company's mobile app becomes unusable for about an hour whenever a marketing campaign is launched.

Courses of Action:
I. Buy additional servers without measuring which part of the application slows down.
II. Ask customers not to use the app during campaign hours.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I spends heavily without knowing where the system fails, so the same collapse may occur again on the new hardware. Course II shifts a technical limitation onto customers and will reduce campaign results. Therefore, neither is a reasonable course of action.

questions.questionText:
The team's automated build pipeline fails randomly in about one run out of five, and developers have to rerun it.

Courses of Action:
I. Reduce the automated tests to those that do not fail randomly.
II. Ask developers to rerun the pipeline until it passes.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I removes the tests that catch defects simply because they are inconvenient, and it lowers the quality of the release. Course II institutionalises the workaround instead of correcting the cause. Therefore, neither course should be followed.

questions.questionText:
The monthly cloud bill has increased by forty per cent over the last two quarters with no growth in users.

Courses of Action:
I. Analyse usage and cost reports, identify idle resources and right-size the instances accordingly.
II. Set monthly budget alerts and review the largest services with the teams that own them.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.
Neither course should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I finds the waste in a measurable way and controls cost. Course II is appropriate because it warns of further increases and places responsibility where the usage is controlled. Therefore, both courses should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
The security team has logged a sharp rise in failed login attempts from an unfamiliar range of foreign IP addresses.

Courses of Action:
I. Investigate the logs, apply rate limiting or blocking as appropriate, and confirm whether any account was compromised.
II. Delete the log entries so that the noise does not continue.
III. Inform the account holders who are being targeted so that they can change their passwords.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Courses I and III should be followed.
None of the courses should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course III should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I treats the suspicious pattern as a possible attack and produces useful evidence. Course II destroys the only record of the attempts. Course III is appropriate because it protects the users who are actually being targeted, in addition to what the investigation establishes. Therefore, courses I and III should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A website takes more than eight seconds to load for users in other countries although it is fast for local users.

Courses of Action:
I. Serve static content through a content-delivery network and optimise the page size.
II. Measure the load time of the site in each target region and track it as a service indicator.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I improves performance for the users who are affected. Course II is appropriate because it verifies the improvement and detects any return of the problem. Therefore, both courses are justified.

questions.questionText:
After a deployment, the error rate of a payment module rises and some transactions fail.

Courses of Action:
I. Ask the support team to retry the failed transactions manually until the next scheduled release.
II. Wait for the next monthly release and fix all errors together.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I leaves a defective payment module in production for a month and relies on manual retries, which the volume of transactions makes impractical. Course II leaves customers unable to complete transactions for a month. Therefore, neither is a reasonable course of action.

questions.questionText:
The company's backup tapes are stored in a cupboard in the same room as the servers.

Courses of Action:
I. Move the backups to a secure off-site location and restart the periodic restore tests.
II. Verify the backups and store a copy off-site so that a single incident cannot destroy both systems and backups.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I does not preserve anything because the backup copies would risk the same incident as the servers. Course II creates genuine protection by separating the copies and proving that they can be restored. Therefore, only course II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A guest has connected to a campus network point and obtained internet access using the same password that staff use for internal systems.

Courses of Action:
I. Allow the practice to continue because the guest caused no damage.
II. Separate the guest network, rotate the shared credentials and give visitors a limited-access account.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course II segments a network that should never have shared credentials and limits future exposure. Course I leaves the same weakness in place for anyone to use. Therefore, course II should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
An employee has installed unlicensed and unapproved software on a company laptop and connected it to the corporate network.

Courses of Action:
I. Remove the unauthorised software, scan the machine and enforce an approved-software policy with a request route.
II. Reformat every laptop in the company immediately.
III. Find out whether an approved alternative is missing or too costly, which is why the software was installed.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: All three courses should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Courses I and III should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I corrects the specific violation and prevents repeats. Course II imposes a costly disruption on users who did nothing wrong. Course III is appropriate because it tests whether a genuine need drove the installation and prevents the same situation from recurring. Therefore, courses I and III should be followed.

questions.questionText:
An administrator's login credentials have appeared in a public code repository.

Courses of Action:
I. Request the code-hosting service to delete the repository so that the credentials are no longer visible.
II. Monitor the account for a month before deciding whether any change is needed.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I removes the public copy but leaves the credential itself valid and the wider exposure unverified. Course II leaves a known credential valid during the observation period. Therefore, neither course is justified.

questions.questionText:
A staff member has opened a document from an unknown sender and enabled macros on a work computer.

Courses of Action:
I. Isolate the computer, scan it, reset the user's credentials if needed and report the incident.
II. Send a short advisory to all staff describing how to recognise such documents and how to report them.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I contains a likely infection and follows the correct incident process. Course II is appropriate because it reduces the chance of another staff member making the same mistake. Therefore, both are reasonable courses of action.

questions.questionText:
A public storage bucket containing internal reports was found to be readable by anyone with the link.

Courses of Action:
I. Make the bucket private immediately, review its contents and audit all similar configurations.
II. Enable logging and alert the team whenever a storage bucket is created with public access.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I closes the exposure and finds other instances of the same misconfiguration. Course II is appropriate because it detects a fresh exposure of the same kind instead of waiting for the next audit. Therefore, both courses I and II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
The database server's disk is ninety-five per cent full and the application is slowing down.

Courses of Action:
I. Archive or purge old logs, expand the volume and set up alerts at defined usage thresholds.
II. Delete the application's transaction tables to free space quickly.
III. Move the entire database to a larger server by the end of the week.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I should be followed.
Only course III should be followed.
Courses I and III should be followed.
None of the courses should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I frees space safely and prevents a recurrence. Course II destroys business data to solve a storage problem, which is far more serious than the problem itself. Course III is a large infrastructure change taken before the growth pattern is understood, and it may only move the same problem to a bigger machine. Therefore, only course I should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Two employees have been sharing their multi-factor authentication codes with each other to cover shifts.

Courses of Action:
I. Issue individual credentials and devices to each role holder and state clearly that codes must not be shared.
II. Explain to the staff why the codes are individual and train supervisors to plan shift cover instead.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.
Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I makes authentication personally accountable and keeps the protection. Course II is appropriate because the practice comes from shift planning, and the supervisors can solve the coverage problem in a compliant way. Therefore, both courses should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
A user has reported a way to view other customers' order details by changing the order number in the website's address.

Courses of Action:
I. Ask the user to keep the finding confidential and take no further steps.
II. Reproduce and fix the access-control error, check the logs for exploitation, and verify other screens for similar flaws.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.

questions.explanationText: Course II fixes a genuine security flaw and checks how widely it may have been abused. Course I conceals a defect that allows customer data to be exposed. Therefore, only course II is justified.

questions.questionText:
The development team has been testing new features with a copy of the live customer database.

Courses of Action:
I. Replace the live data in test systems with anonymised data and restrict access to production copies.
II. Restrict access to copies of production data to a small named group with recorded approvals.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I removes the exposure of personal data as a matter of process. Course II is appropriate because it limits who can reach customer data even in the systems where it must exist. Therefore, both are reasonable courses of action.

questions.questionText:
Login attempts on the customer portal do not slow down even after hundreds of wrong passwords from the same source.

Courses of Action:
I. Add rate limiting and temporary lockouts to the login service and monitor the pattern.
II. Log the source addresses of the repeated failures and review them with the security team every week.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I prevents automated guessing and is directly relevant to the observed behaviour. Course II is appropriate because it builds a record of the attempts and lets the team decide on blocking with evidence. Therefore, both courses I and II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Only one person in the company understands how to perform the month-end data reconciliation, and that person is going on three weeks' leave.

Courses of Action:
I. Document the procedure with the role holder, train a second person and run the process jointly once.
II. Add the reconciliation to the role description of a second post so that two people are always trained.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.
Neither course should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I removes the dependency and keeps the business process on schedule. Course II is appropriate because it removes the dependence on one individual in the future rather than for one leave period only. Therefore, both courses should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
The company's laptops are not encrypted, and one laptop has been stolen from a car.

Courses of Action:
I. Remotely wipe the device if possible, notify the affected users and enforce disk encryption on all laptops.
II. Report the theft to the police and record the incident so that the affected users can be told what data were at risk.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I responds to the theft and closes the broader exposure of unencrypted devices. Course II is appropriate because it follows the correct reporting route and identifies whose information is affected. Therefore, both courses are justified.

questions.questionText:
Employees are using personal email accounts to send internal files because the corporate system has size limits.

Courses of Action:
I. Provide an approved file-sharing service for large files and set out a clear policy on data handling.
II. Review the size limit of the corporate file service so that the documents are no longer sent through personal accounts.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I gives staff a compliant route for a legitimate need. Course II is appropriate because it removes the practical reason that staff are turning to personal email. Therefore, both are reasonable courses of action.

questions.questionText:
A security assessment found that access rights in the finance system have accumulated over the years and many users have rights beyond their current roles.

Courses of Action:
I. Review entitlements against current job roles, revoke what is unnecessary and introduce periodic access reviews.
II. Reset every user's rights to the minimum and ask users to request access again individually.
III. Give the security team a report of accounts that have not been used for ninety days so that they can be deactivated.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Courses I and III should be followed.
None of the courses should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course III should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I corrects excessive access in a planned way without stopping work. Course II causes an avoidable operational breakdown because it revokes access indiscriminately and at once. Course III is appropriate because dormant accounts are a common route for misuse and the report can be produced from logs that already exist. Therefore, courses I and III should be followed.

questions.questionText:
The organisation has decided to introduce two-factor authentication, but support calls about resets have overwhelmed the help desk during the first week.

Courses of Action:
I. Cancel the two-factor authentication project because it causes inconvenience.
II. Roll out the change department by department, publish simple guidance and add temporary help-desk capacity.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course II manages a worthwhile change in a way that users and the help desk can absorb. Course I abandons a security improvement because of a temporary process problem. Therefore, only course II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A third-party vendor has remote access to the company's systems, and the contract does not state how that access must be controlled.

Courses of Action:
I. Review the contract, apply least-privilege access with time-limited connections and log vendor activity.
II. Require vendor access to be opened only for agreed hours and closed immediately afterwards.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.
Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I controls a real risk while keeping a necessary business relationship. Course II is appropriate because it limits the vendor's access to the periods in which work is scheduled. Therefore, both courses should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
The company's website is being flooded with requests that have caused intermittent outages over two days.

Courses of Action:
I. Shut down the website until the traffic stops.
II. Engage the internet service provider or a traffic-filtering service, apply rate limits and publish service updates to customers.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course II mitigates the flood while keeping the service available for genuine customers. Course I surrenders the service to the attacker, which is exactly the outcome the person flooding it wants. Therefore, only course II is justified.

questions.questionText:
An internal tool that is used daily contains a library with a security flaw disclosed last month; the team has no time to upgrade it.

Courses of Action:
I. Assess the exposure, apply the vendor's patch or a targeted mitigation, and schedule the full upgrade in the next sprint.
II. Record the risk in the project's register with an owner and a target date for the upgrade.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I addresses the exposure immediately and plans the proper fix. Course II is appropriate because it keeps the unpatched dependency visible and tracked until the full upgrade is done. Therefore, both are reasonable courses of action.

questions.questionText:
The office network is being monitored, and logs show large volumes of data being transferred to an external address every night at two o'clock.

Courses of Action:
I. Wait for the next quarterly audit before examining the transfers.
II. Investigate the source and destination of the transfers, contain the affected systems and inform the incident-response team.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course II treats unexplained outbound traffic as a possible incident and contains it quickly. Course I allows a suspicious pattern to continue for months. Therefore, only course II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A company's disaster-recovery plan has never been tested and the team is unsure how long a full restoration would take.

Courses of Action:
I. Declare the plan complete because it exists on paper.
II. Run a planned recovery exercise on a replica environment, measure the timings and update the plan.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course II proves the plan works and gives the recovery times the business needs for planning. Course I leaves an untested plan while assuming it is adequate. Therefore, course II should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
A college's online examination platform crashed during the first ten minutes of a test, and students had to be rescheduled.

Courses of Action:
I. Re-run the affected students' tests on a repaired platform, investigate the failure and load-test the platform before the next examination.
II. Prepare a contingency plan that sets out how candidates will be rescheduled if the platform fails again.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I restores the assessment and prevents a repetition. Course II is appropriate because it prepares the institution to respond if the examination platform fails during a session. Therefore, both courses are justified.

questions.questionText:
Rumours of a data breach are circulating on social media, although no confirmed breach has been identified so far.

Courses of Action:
I. Deny the incident publicly before any technical verification has been done.
II. Verify the claim from logs and systems, and issue an accurate holding statement while the check is under way.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course II establishes the facts and communicates responsibly during the check. Course I commits the company to a claim that may prove false and destroys trust. Therefore, course II is the better course of action.

questions.questionText:
Employees have reported that the internal knowledge portal contains outdated installation guides that lead to errors.

Courses of Action:
I. Assign an owner for each guide, mark the version and date, and set a review cycle for critical documents.
II. Make the updating of each guide part of the process whenever the tool or the version changes.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I corrects the unreliable content at source. Course II is appropriate because it keeps the documents correct without a separate clean-up effort. Therefore, both courses I and II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
The information-technology team receives about sixty password-reset calls every week.

Courses of Action:
I. Introduce self-service password reset with secure identity verification and publish the steps.
II. Publish a short guide on choosing memorable passphrases so that users reset to stronger passwords.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.
Neither course should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I cuts the workload by removing its cause while keeping the process secure. Course II is appropriate because it reduces the number of resets by helping users pick passwords they can remember. Therefore, both courses should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
