A bug was reported in a financial report that the company sends to clients, and the error was traced to an incorrect formula.

Courses of Action:
I. Wait for the next reporting cycle since only one report was affected.
II. Correct the formula, reissue the reports to the affected clients and add validation checks to the reporting process.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.

questions.explanationText: Course II corrects the inaccurate information that clients rely on and prevents a repeat. Course I leaves incorrect financial information in the clients' hands. Therefore, only course II is justified.

questions.questionText:
A team has been asked to reduce the time taken to deploy software, which currently takes two days of manual steps.

Courses of Action:
I. Automate the build, test and release steps gradually and document each stage.
II. Ask developers to work at night so that deployments finish sooner.
III. Require every deployment to be approved by two managers before it can start.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course II should be followed.
Courses I and III should be followed.
All three courses should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I removes the manual effort that makes deployments slow. Course II adds a burden to staff without changing the process that causes the delay. Course III adds approval steps to a process that is already slow and would increase the delay it is meant to reduce. Therefore, only course I should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A library of open-source code used across many projects has been abandoned by its maintainers.

Courses of Action:
I. Continue to use the library indefinitely without any change because it still works.
II. Assess the risk, plan a migration path to a supported alternative and monitor the current version in the meantime.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course II manages a known long-term risk with a practical plan. Course I accepts an unmanaged dependency that will eventually become a serious problem. Therefore, course II is the better course of action.

questions.questionText:
Customers report that the mobile app logs them out repeatedly, and the first support response is that users should reinstall the app each time.

Courses of Action:
I. Continue advising customers to reinstall the app on every occurrence.
II. Reproduce the issue from the application logs, fix the session-handling defect and publish a corrected release.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course II removes the defect that causes the repeated logout. Course I keeps a workaround that puts the cost of the fault on the customer. Therefore, only course II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A company stores customer card details in a spreadsheet on a shared drive for convenience.

Courses of Action:
I. Stop storing card data in the spreadsheet, use the approved payment system and delete the existing copies securely.
II. Brief the team on which data may be stored locally and where customer information must be handled.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.
Neither course should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I removes the exposure of sensitive payment data. Course II is appropriate because the staff need to know clearly which records must never be kept outside the approved systems. Therefore, both courses should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
Two students have gained access to the examination question paper stored on a college server before the examination.

Courses of Action:
I. Change the paper at the last moment without telling anyone why.
II. Secure the paper, notify the examination authority immediately and run an investigation with log evidence.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course II handles a breach of examination security through the proper authority and preserves the evidence. Course I conceals the incident and leaves the access route open. Therefore, only course II is justified.

questions.questionText:
An internet-of-things sensor network on an industrial campus uses default passwords that were never changed.

Courses of Action:
I. Leave the devices alone because they are not connected to business systems.
II. Change the credentials at once, isolate the sensor network and add a standard configuration checklist for new devices.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course II closes the weakness and prevents its repetition on new devices. Course I rests on an assumption about the network layout that has not been verified. Therefore, course II is the better course of action.

questions.questionText:
A company's support staff share one admin account because individual accounts were said to be inconvenient.

Courses of Action:
I. Create individual accounts with role-based permissions, record activity and retire the shared account.
II. Provide a request process through which staff can obtain the extra rights only for the time they are needed.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I makes activity traceable and applies proper access control. Course II is appropriate because it removes the reason the shared account was created. Therefore, both courses I and II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A software company finds that the same type of defect has escaped to customers in three successive releases.

Courses of Action:
I. Ask the quality team to test more manually before each release without changing the process.
II. Add automated tests and a review gate that target that defect class before release.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.
Neither course should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course II addresses the pattern that allows the defect to escape repeatedly. Course I increases effort in the same process without correcting the weakness that let the defects through. Therefore, course II should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
Employees working from home report repeated disconnections during video meetings, and there is no formal standard for remote connectivity.

Courses of Action:
I. Publish minimum connectivity and equipment standards, and provide an approved secure remote-access method.
II. Ban work from home to avoid the connectivity complaints.
III. Pay a monthly connectivity allowance to staff who regularly work from home.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Courses I and III should be followed.
All three courses should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Courses I and II should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I sets standards and provides the tools for a working arrangement the company already uses. Course II withdraws a working model instead of correcting the conditions that make it difficult. Course III is appropriate because it removes the cost barrier that stops staff from maintaining a connection which meets the standard. Therefore, courses I and III should be followed.

questions.questionText:
An office printer is shared by all staff, and confidential documents are frequently left in the output tray.

Courses of Action:
I. Remove the printer and ask all staff to buy their own devices.
II. Enable badge-based secure printing so that jobs are released only by the person who sent them.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course II prevents the documents being left exposed. Course I creates an unnecessary cost and inconvenience for a problem that has a simple technical solution. Therefore, only course II is justified.

questions.questionText:
Ransomware has encrypted files on a shared drive used by the accounts department, and a message demands payment.

Courses of Action:
I. Collect the payment quickly and continue working with the same systems.
II. Isolate the affected systems, restore the affected data from verified backups and report the incident to the authorities and security team.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.

questions.explanationText: Course II contains the incident, restores the data through legitimate means and follows the correct reporting route. Course I funds criminal activity, does not guarantee recovery and leaves the systems compromised. Therefore, course II is the better course of action.

questions.questionText:
During a shift change, two technicians both believed the other had taken the backup of the day's data, and no backup was made.

Courses of Action:
I. Introduce a signed handover checklist for backups and add automated verification that the backup exists.
II. Ask both technicians to check the backup again the next morning.
III. Appoint a third technician to watch the backup every evening.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: All three courses should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Courses I and II should be followed.
Courses II and III should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I removes the gap in responsibility and adds a technical check. Course II repeats the same informal practice that allowed the backup to be missed. Course III adds supervision instead of closing the handover gap, and the same confusion would return whenever that person is absent. Therefore, only course I should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Sales in the western region have fallen by thirty per cent over six months although sales in other regions are steady.

Courses of Action:
I. Reduce the prices of all products across the country by twenty per cent.
II. Survey customers and dealers in the western region to identify local reasons and draw up a region-specific plan.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I is a country-wide reaction to a regional problem and would reduce revenue everywhere. Course II first establishes the local cause and then plans action, which is the practical response. Therefore, only course II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Customer complaints about a newly launched appliance have risen sharply in the first month.

Courses of Action:
I. Ask the customers to send the appliance to the service centre at their own cost.
II. Extend the warranty period of the appliance by one year.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I places the effort and cost of a product fault on the customers and does nothing to remove that fault from the product. Course II compensates customers but leaves the faulty product in the market, so complaints would continue. Therefore, neither course should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
The night shift of a factory has lost nearly half its workers through resignations in the last year.

Courses of Action:
I. Hold exit interviews and a staff survey to find out what drives the resignations, then correct the specific causes.
II. Review the night-shift allowance and the transport arrangements against what similar firms provide.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I identifies and removes the reason people are leaving. Course II is appropriate because pay and travel are among the practical reasons night-shift staff leave. Therefore, both courses are justified.

questions.questionText:
A retail chain ran out of its best-selling items during the festival season for the second consecutive year.

Courses of Action:
I. Analyse the previous seasons' sales data, set reorder levels accordingly and place orders earlier.
II. Track promised delivery dates from suppliers during the festival period and follow up on the shortest lead times.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I reduces the chance of another shortage using information the chain already has. Course II is appropriate because it keeps the supply predictable during the weeks when demand is highest. Therefore, both are reasonable courses of action.

questions.questionText:
A manufacturer depends on a single supplier for a critical component, and the supplier has delayed three shipments this year.

Courses of Action:
I. Qualify a second supplier and hold a small buffer stock of the critical component.
II. Terminate the existing supplier with immediate effect and buy from whoever is available.
III. Include a delivery-performance clause with agreed consequences in future supplier agreements.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Courses I and III should be followed.
All three courses should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I reduces the risk of dependence while keeping the supply running. Course II creates an immediate shortage without any assured alternative. Course III is appropriate because it improves supplier performance through the agreement itself and can be applied to every future contract. Therefore, courses I and III should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Operating costs of a service company have risen faster than revenue for two years.

Courses of Action:
I. Conduct a cost audit, identify the largest cost growth areas and remove waste before considering any broad cuts.
II. Hold a quarterly review of the largest cost lines with the departments that own them.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I targets inefficiency with evidence. Course II is appropriate because it keeps the cost trends visible and fixes responsibility for them. Therefore, both courses I and II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
The average time taken to answer a customer support call has increased to twenty minutes.

Courses of Action:
I. Measure call volumes by time of day, add staff during peak periods and publish a response target.
II. Automatically close all calls that are unanswered after five minutes.
III. Introduce a multi-level automated menu that the caller must pass through before reaching an agent.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Courses II and III should be followed.
None of the courses should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I matches staffing to demand and improves the service measured. Course II manipulates the measurement while leaving customers without help. Course III adds steps to the caller's journey and would increase the time taken rather than reduce it. Therefore, only course I should be followed.

questions.questionText:
The company's production line stops three or four times a week because of ageing machinery, and each stop lasts about two hours.

Courses of Action:
I. Publish the schedule of the stoppages on the notice board for the production staff.
II. Replace the entire production line immediately with new equipment.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I records the breakdowns without reducing them, so the idle time would continue. Course II requires a large investment before the actual failure pattern is known and would idle the plant during installation. Therefore, neither course should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
Ratings of a company's product on online marketplaces have dropped because several buyers complained of poor after-sales service.

Courses of Action:
I. Review the service process, respond to the complaints individually and improve the turnaround of service requests.
II. Set a service response target and publish it to customers.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I corrects the service that caused the poor ratings. Course II is appropriate because it gives customers a clear expectation and makes the service performance measurable. Therefore, both courses are justified.

questions.questionText:
Quality-control rejection in a factory has risen from two per cent to seven per cent in three months with the same machinery and materials.

Courses of Action:
I. Analyse rejection data by machine, shift and operator, and retrain the groups where the defects cluster.
II. Track the rejections by machine so that the worst-performing machine is identified.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I locates the source of the variation before acting. Course II is appropriate because it locates the source of the variation before any wider change is made. Therefore, both are reasonable courses of action.

questions.questionText:
An important client has complained of delayed deliveries and has hinted that it may move to a competitor.

Courses of Action:
I. Assign a senior manager to review the client's delivery issues, agree a recovery plan and monitor it weekly.
II. Assign a delivery coordinator for this client's orders so that delays are caught before dispatch.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I addresses the specific problem of the client who is at risk. Course II is appropriate because it fixes the deliveries that the client is actually complaining about. Therefore, both courses I and II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A software project has been running two weeks behind schedule for the last two months.

Courses of Action:
I. Re-plan the remaining scope with the client, agree on priorities and communicate the revised dates honestly.
II. Track the remaining work with weekly milestones so that any slippage becomes visible early.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both courses should be implemented.
Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I brings the schedule under control with the client's agreement. Course II is appropriate because weekly tracking shows a slip early enough for the schedule to be corrected. Therefore, both courses should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
Productivity in a design team has been falling, and the same tasks now take almost twice as long as they did last year.

Courses of Action:
I. Extend the working day by two hours for the whole team.
II. Review the workflow, tools and workload of the team to locate the bottleneck before changing the working hours.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course II looks for the reason that output has slowed. Course I increases hours without knowing the cause, which would lower morale and may worsen productivity further. Therefore, only course II is justified.

questions.questionText:
Orders dispatched from a warehouse are frequently sent with the wrong item.

Courses of Action:
I. Increase the dispatch target for each picker so that the staff work faster and clear the pending orders.
II. Issue a warning letter to every worker in the warehouse.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I presses the pickers to work faster, which is likely to increase the very errors that are being reported. Course II punishes everyone without correcting the process that allows the errors. Therefore, neither is a reasonable course of action.

questions.questionText:
The sales team has stopped updating the new customer-relationship system, so management reports are unreliable.

Courses of Action:
I. Find out why the system is not usable in the field, simplify the entry process and train the team on the workflow.
II. Reduce the fields that must be entered to those the sales process actually needs.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I corrects the adoption problem and keeps the reporting benefit. Course II is appropriate because it removes the effort that makes the sales team avoid the system. Therefore, both courses I and II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A competitor has reduced its prices and the company has lost a share of the market in that segment.

Courses of Action:
I. Examine the cost structure and customer priorities to decide whether a targeted response is possible without selling below cost.
II. Ask the sales team to record the reason for every loss so that any price response is based on evidence.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I bases the response on the company's own economics. Course II is appropriate because it builds the evidence the company needs before committing to a pricing decision. Therefore, both courses should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
Marketing spending has doubled over two years while sales have remained flat.

Courses of Action:
I. Measure the return of each marketing channel, stop the ineffective ones and re-allocate the budget on evidence.
II. Set a cost-per-acquisition target for each channel and review it every month.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I uses measurement to correct an unproductive trend. Course II is appropriate because it gives the team a measurable standard for judging each channel. Therefore, both courses are justified.

questions.questionText:
Several employees have complained that the shift roster is drawn up without notice and without considering their requests.

Courses of Action:
I. Allow employees to arrange shifts among themselves without any record.
II. Publish the roster at least a week in advance and set a clear, fair process for shift-change requests.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.

questions.explanationText: Course II gives predictability and a fair procedure. Course I removes the planning process altogether and would create coverage gaps. Therefore, course II is the better course of action.

questions.questionText:
Sales reports show that many deals are lost at the final pricing stage, where approvals take more than a week.

Courses of Action:
I. Review the approval limits and delegate decision rights so that standard discounts are approved quickly.
II. Discontinue the product line that loses the most deals on price.
III. Publish a standard discount matrix so that the sales team knows which offers need no approval.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Courses I and III should be followed.
None of the courses should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course III should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I removes the delay that is losing the deals. Course II removes a product because of an administrative bottleneck. Course III is appropriate because it removes the need for approval in routine cases and shortens the time taken to close a deal. Therefore, courses I and III should be followed.

questions.questionText:
An online store receives many complaints that parcels arrive damaged.

Courses of Action:
I. Review the packaging and carrier handling, strengthen the packaging for fragile items and track damage rates.
II. Record damage claims by carrier and route so that the worst performers can be reviewed.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I reduces damage at its source. Course II is appropriate because it shows where the damage is occurring and supports a discussion with the carrier. Therefore, both courses I and II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Employees have not taken their accumulated leave for two years because of continuous project pressure.

Courses of Action:
I. Review workloads and staffing so that planned leave can be scheduled without disrupting projects.
II. Track leave balances by team and flag any team in which leave has not been taken for two quarters.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.
Neither course should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I removes the workload reason that prevents leave. Course II is appropriate because it brings the problem to the notice of the managers who can plan for it. Therefore, both courses should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
Workers have complained about hygiene in the factory canteen.

Courses of Action:
I. Have the canteen inspected against standards, publish the findings and require the vendor to correct them.
II. Include a worker representative in the periodic canteen inspection.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I rectifies the deficiencies through an inspection with follow-up. Course II is appropriate because it brings the users of the canteen into the inspection and makes the follow-up credible. Therefore, both courses are justified.

questions.questionText:
Idle time on a production floor has increased because maintenance is carried out only after machines break down.

Courses of Action:
I. Run all machines at half speed indefinitely so that they break down less often.
II. Move to a planned preventive-maintenance schedule with periodic checks and spare-part planning.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course II prevents breakdowns and the idle time they cause. Course I permanently reduces capacity and is not a maintenance solution. Therefore, course II is the better course of action.

questions.questionText:
The electricity bill of a plant has risen by twenty-five per cent without any increase in production.

Courses of Action:
I. Conduct an energy audit, fix compressed-air and motor inefficiencies, and monitor consumption by area.
II. Install sub-meters in the major consumption areas so that the usage becomes visible.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I cuts consumption without touching output. Course II is appropriate because it shows where the electricity is being used before any equipment is replaced. Therefore, both courses I and II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Absenteeism in a manufacturing unit is highest on Mondays and after pay-day.

Courses of Action:
I. Speak to the affected groups to understand the pattern and address issues such as transport or health in those groups.
II. Track attendance by shift and by day so that the effect of any measure can be verified.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.
Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I investigates a recognisable pattern before acting. Course II is appropriate because it shows whether the steps taken actually improve attendance. Therefore, both courses should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
Invoices from suppliers frequently show quantities and rates that do not match the purchase orders.

Courses of Action:
I. Ask the suppliers to correct their invoices and resubmit them.
II. Pause payments to every supplier until the accounts are audited.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I deals with the faulty invoices one by one but leaves the company without the verification step that would catch the errors before payment. Course II disrupts all suppliers and would harm the company's own supply chain. Therefore, neither course is justified.

questions.questionText:
Customer-satisfaction scores are low mainly because users find the product's settings difficult to understand.

Courses of Action:
I. Include a day of training in the price of every unit so that each customer learns the settings.
II. Tell customers that the settings are meant for advanced users and require no change.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I charges every customer for training to overcome a difficulty that the product itself creates. Course II dismisses the complaint and leaves the difficulty in place. Therefore, neither is a reasonable course of action.

questions.questionText:
Two departments blame each other for delays in approving new products, and both have incomplete records of the process.

Courses of Action:
I. Map the approval process jointly with both departments, fix the hand-off points and name a single owner for each stage.
II. Hold a joint weekly review of the pending approvals with both departments present.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I corrects the process and the unclear ownership that produce the delays. Course II is appropriate because a joint review resolves the hand-off problems as they occur. Therefore, both courses I and II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A store keeps running out of its ten highest-selling items while slow-moving stock accumulates.

Courses of Action:
I. Use sales data to set reorder points for the fast movers and clear the slow-moving stock through a planned clearance.
II. Order a large quantity of every item so that no product is ever short.
III. Order every item only when its stock falls below one common level fixed for all products.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Courses I and II should be followed.
All three courses should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I aligns stock with demand and releases blocked working capital. Course II increases holding costs and the volume of unsold stock. Course III applies a single stock level to products with very different turnover and would leave the fast movers short while the slow movers pile up. Therefore, only course I should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Staff must work with a new technology platform, but most of them have not been trained on it.

Courses of Action:
I. Recruit senior staff from outside to handle the platform so that the existing team can continue as before.
II. Run role-based training with a practice environment before the full rollout.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.
Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course II builds the capability of the existing team in a practical way. Course I is an expensive and slow response to a training gap that can be closed directly. Therefore, course II should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
A company plans to move its office to a new location twenty kilometres away, and employees have begun discussing resignations.

Courses of Action:
I. Share the relocation plan with staff early, explain the reasons and provide transport support or phased transition.
II. Announce the relocation only after the new premises are occupied.
III. Survey the staff to find which functions the move would affect most and sequence the relocation team by team.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: All three courses should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Courses I and II should be followed.
Courses I and III should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I reduces the uncertainty that drives the attrition risk. Course II guarantees that the concern builds up without any response from the company. Course III is appropriate because it identifies which teams need the most support and allows the move to be planned in stages. Therefore, courses I and III should be followed.

questions.questionText:
An internal audit has found that production records are incomplete and are completed after the shift ends from memory.

Courses of Action:
I. Appoint an additional clerk to write the records for all the shifts.
II. Ask the supervisors to be careful while writing the records at the end of the shift.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I adds a person to record data that only those at the machine can know accurately, so the record would remain second-hand. Course II leaves the same process in place and depends on increased care alone. Therefore, neither course is justified.

questions.questionText:
Sales targets for the year have been set at four times last year's performance for every territory.

Courses of Action:
I. Recruit more sales staff for every territory so that the higher targets are met by a larger team.
II. Keep the targets unchanged and warn the sales staff that failure will affect their appraisal.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I adds cost in every territory without examining whether the targets themselves are achievable, which is the question that has been raised. Course II preserves targets that are not related to the market and would demotivate the team. Therefore, neither is a reasonable course of action.

questions.questionText:
A suggestion scheme in a factory has received no proposals in a year.

Courses of Action:
I. Reply to the earlier suggestions that have not been acted upon and publicise the changes that resulted from them.
II. Close the suggestion scheme since employees are not interested.
III. Ask the supervisors to submit suggestions on behalf of their teams.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Courses I and III should be followed.
None of the courses should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course III should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I rebuilds credibility in the scheme, which is the likely reason for the silence. Course II removes the channel rather than restoring the employees' confidence in it. Course III collects ideas from supervisors rather than from the employees the scheme is meant for, and it does not restore confidence in the scheme. Therefore, only course I should be followed.

questions.questionText:
The packaging cost of a product has risen and the marketing team wants to use thinner material to save money.

Courses of Action:
I. Test thinner alternatives against transit-damage standards before deciding, and review the pack size at the same time.
II. Compare the cost of thinner packaging with the cost of damage and returns before finalising the change.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I reduces cost while checking that damage rates do not rise. Course II is appropriate because the decision should weigh the packing saving against the return costs it may cause. Therefore, both courses I and II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Shoplifting has increased in a retail store over the last quarter.

Courses of Action:
I. Display notices in the store stating that shoplifting is a punishable offence.
II. Search every customer physically before they leave the store.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.
Neither course should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I relies on a notice to change behaviour and leaves the store layout and surveillance exactly as they were. Course II would humiliate customers and damage the store's reputation without addressing the actual weakness. Therefore, neither course should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
Salaries in a small firm are often paid a week late because payroll is computed manually in spreadsheets.

Courses of Action:
I. Move payroll to a standard system with defined cut-off dates and communicate the new schedule.
II. Publish a payroll calendar so that staff know the payment date each month.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I removes the manual process that causes the delay. Course II is appropriate because it gives the staff a schedule they can rely on while the system is replaced. Therefore, both courses are justified.

questions.questionText:
A manufacturer has found that the same component supplier has sent out-of-specification material three times this year.

Courses of Action:
I. Rate suppliers on quality, record the deviations and require a formal corrective-action plan from the supplier.
II. Cancel all contracts with every supplier and buy from the open market.
III. Increase the inspection sampling of incoming material from that supplier until its quality improves.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Courses I and III should be followed.
All three courses should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I addresses the supply quality with a measurable control. Course II destroys the supply base without dealing with the specific problem. Course III is appropriate as an immediate control that keeps defective material out while the supplier's process is corrected. Therefore, courses I and III should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A newly launched product has not met its sales targets in six months, and the company is considering what to do.

Courses of Action:
I. Gather customer feedback and usage data to identify why buyers are not choosing it, then adjust the product or its positioning.
II. Run a survey of the buyers who considered the product but did not purchase it.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I works out why the product is not selling before deciding its fate. Course II is appropriate because the reasons for non-purchase are exactly what the review needs. Therefore, both are reasonable courses of action.

questions.questionText:
Employees have complained that their job responsibilities overlap with those of another role, and decisions often stall.

Courses of Action:
I. Define role charters with decision rights, review them with the teams and resolve the overlaps.
II. Merge the two roles into one so that the overlap disappears.
III. Publish a chart showing which employee reports to which manager.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: All three courses should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Courses I and III should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I settles the ambiguity that causes the stalls. Course II may create a workload problem and does not establish who decides what. Course III clarifies the reporting lines but leaves the overlapping responsibilities themselves unresolved, so decisions would still stall. Therefore, only course I should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Customer support tickets are frequently reopened because the first reply does not solve the problem.

Courses of Action:
I. Analyse the reopened tickets, correct the knowledge base and retrain the team on the categories that fail most.
II. Stop measuring the number of reopened tickets so that the reports look better.
III. Increase the number of tickets each agent must close every day.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Courses I and II should be followed.
All three courses should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I improves the quality of the first response. Course II hides the measurement that reveals the problem. Course III raises the volume target that is already causing hurried replies and would make the quality problem worse. Therefore, only course I should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A customer's complaint about a defective product has been shared widely on social media within a day.

Courses of Action:
I. Contact the customer, resolve the specific complaint and publish a clear statement about the action taken.
II. Delete the complaint from the company's social pages and block the customer.
III. Issue a general statement that the company stands by the quality of all its products.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Courses II and III should be followed.
All three courses should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Courses I and II should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I addresses the cause of the complaint and the public concern. Course II would intensify the criticism and appear to hide the problem. Course III defends the product in general terms instead of answering the customer's complaint, and it would increase the criticism rather than settle it. Therefore, only course I should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A factory's output falls on the first working day after each pay-day.

Courses of Action:
I. Close the factory on that day every month so that no one is absent.
II. Cut the pay of all workers who are absent on that day without any enquiry.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I answers absence by stopping production on the day altogether, which harms output more than the absence does. Course II applies a penalty that may be unfair in individual cases and would not correct the pattern by itself. Therefore, neither course should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A branch of a bank has consistently lower productivity than other branches of the same size.

Courses of Action:
I. Close the branch and transfer its customers to the nearest branch.
II. Review staffing, workload mix and processes of that branch against comparable branches and act on the gaps found.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course II compares the branch with similar ones and identifies correctable gaps. Course I removes a service point and burdens customers before any attempt to improve the branch. Therefore, course II should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
Customers have complained that the amounts on their monthly utility-style bills do not match their usage records.

Courses of Action:
I. Reconcile the billing data with the meter records, correct the errors and automate the reconciliation step.
II. Reduce the frequency of bills so that errors appear less often.
III. Stop issuing bills for three months while the billing system is corrected.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I should be followed.
Only course III should be followed.
Courses I and III should be followed.
None of the courses should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I corrects the errors customers are facing. Course II would leave the same faults in every bill, whatever the frequency. Course III interrupts the billing cycle altogether and would create a cash-flow problem far larger than the errors being corrected. Therefore, only course I should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A sales team's travel expenses have increased sharply, and some claims do not match the schedule of customer visits.

Courses of Action:
I. Tighten the expense policy, verify claims against visit records and audit a sample of past claims.
II. Publish a clear claim policy with the documents required for each type of expense.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I addresses the misuse without stopping legitimate travel. Course II is appropriate because it tells staff what is acceptable and makes verification straightforward. Therefore, both courses are justified.

questions.questionText:
Nearly a third of the employees recruited last year left within four months of joining.

Courses of Action:
I. Improve the onboarding and mentoring process and collect feedback from recent leavers to correct the early experience.
II. Require every new employee to sign a service bond of two years.
III. Assign a mentor to every new joiner for the first three months with a fortnightly review.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course III should be followed.
Courses I and III should be followed.
None of the courses should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I fixes the early experience that is driving new joiners away. Course II compels people to stay, which does not create commitment and would affect recruitment. Course III is appropriate because it gives new employees a point of contact during exactly the period in which they are leaving. Therefore, courses I and III should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A product's user manual contains several steps that no longer match the current version of the software.

Courses of Action:
I. Ask users to post questions online and rely on community answers for the differences.
II. Update the manual with the release process, and make each release include a documentation check.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course II keeps documentation accurate as part of the release cycle. Course I leaves the official material incorrect and depends on customers to correct it. Therefore, course II is the better course of action.

questions.questionText:
A production plant has a defect rate of six per cent while the accepted standard for the industry is two per cent.

Courses of Action:
I. Study the defects by process stage, fix the largest contributors and train operators on the changed methods.
II. Add a second inspection stage at the end of the line so that defective items are caught before dispatch.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I attacks the causes of the defects at the stage where they are produced. Course II prevents defective items reaching customers. Both are legitimate and address different parts of the same problem. Therefore, both courses I and II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A company is losing business to a competitor that delivers faster.

Courses of Action:
I. Increase the selling price of all products to recover lost revenue.
II. Sue the competitor for unfair trade practice without evidence of any violation.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.
Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I is unrelated to the reason for the losses and would make the company less competitive. Course II is a legal step with no basis in the information given and would not improve delivery. Neither addresses the stated problem. Therefore, neither course should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
An information-technology services firm has lost three clients in a year, mainly on complaints about delivery quality.

Courses of Action:
I. Set up a delivery-quality review that tracks commitments at each project stage.
II. Fund certification of the company's processes against a recognised quality standard.
III. Raise the billing rates for all new contracts to improve revenue.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: All three courses should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Courses II and III should be followed.
Courses I and II should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Courses I and II both strengthen delivery quality, which is the reason clients are leaving, and both are practical for a growing firm. Course III deals with revenue rather than quality and would make the firm less attractive to the clients it is losing. Therefore, courses I and II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A retail chain's margins are falling even though sales volumes are steady.

Courses of Action:
I. Renegotiate terms with suppliers on the basis of purchase volumes.
II. Reduce wastage and shrinkage through tighter stock control.
III. Cut all staff salaries by forty per cent with immediate effect.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: All three courses should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Courses I and II should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Courses I and II improve margin by reducing cost and loss in a manageable way. Course III is a drastic measure that would damage morale, break trust and may not even be legal without following due process, so it is not an appropriate first response. Therefore, courses I and II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A start-up's application has become slow and simultaneously the sales team says it is losing deals because features are missing.

Courses of Action:
I. Profile the slowest components and fix the performance bottlenecks.
II. Prioritise the top three missing features that the sales team reports most often and plan the rest.
III. Reduce the development team's size to conserve cash.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Courses I and II should be followed.
Courses II and III should be followed.
All three courses should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Courses I and II address the two problems that are actually limiting the business: performance and missing features. Course III reduces the team's capacity to solve either problem and would worsen both. Therefore, courses I and II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Four accidents have occurred in two months on a road stretch near a curve, all after dark.

Courses of Action:
I. Ban all traffic on that road between eight in the evening and six in the morning.
II. Advise drivers through the local radio to avoid the stretch at night.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I removes the road from use for the hours in which people need it and does not correct the hazard. Course II asks drivers to avoid a public road instead of correcting the hazard, so the stretch would remain dangerous for those who must use it. Therefore, neither course is justified.

questions.questionText:
Deep potholes have appeared on a busy city road after the monsoon and two-wheelers are skidding.

Courses of Action:
I. Barricade the affected stretch, fill the potholes on priority and collect rain damage reports across the zone.
II. Wait for the annual resurfacing contract before any repair is done.
III. Impose a temporary speed restriction with warning boards on the affected stretch until the repairs are complete.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course II should be followed.
Courses I and III should be followed.
All three courses should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I removes the immediate danger to road users and deals with similar damage in the same locality. Course II leaves a hazardous road untreated for months. Course III is appropriate as an immediate safety measure while the permanent repairs are carried out. Therefore, courses I and III should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A road bridge in a rural district has developed visible cracks and carries heavy trucks every day.

Courses of Action:
I. Close the bridge permanently and ask road users to take a detour of forty kilometres.
II. Restrict heavy vehicles on the bridge and arrange a structural inspection at the earliest opportunity.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course II reduces the load on a structure of doubtful safety while an expert assessment is arranged. Course I is an extreme step that would isolate the locality before the condition of the bridge is even known. Therefore, course II is the better course of action.

questions.questionText:
Traffic backs up for almost a kilometre at the college gate every morning as students and staff arrive at the same time.

Courses of Action:
I. Close the main gate and allow entry only through a side gate without any traffic arrangement.
II. Stagger the reporting times of departments and deploy trained traffic wardens at the gate during peak hours.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course II spreads the arrival peak and manages the junction where the congestion occurs. Course I moves the problem to another entrance without managing the flow of vehicles. Therefore, only course II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Streetlights in a residential block have been out for three weeks and residents avoid walking there at night.

Courses of Action:
I. Send one letter to the electrical authority and wait for the annual maintenance cycle to restore the lights.
II. Advise residents to avoid going out after dark until the lights are repaired.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I accepts three weeks of darkness in a residential block and leaves the residents with neither light nor a follow-up. Course II asks the public to bear the consequence of a fault instead of getting it corrected. Therefore, neither course should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
A village receives piped water on only two days a week because nearly half the supply is lost through leaks.

Courses of Action:
I. Repair the leaking distribution lines and audit the losses while arranging water tankers in the interim.
II. Restrict supply to the main street and let other areas manage on their own.
III. Install bulk meters at the distribution points so that the losses can be measured and localised.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Courses I and II should be followed.
Courses I and III should be followed.
All three courses should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I recovers the lost water and helps the village in the short term. Course II creates unfair access and leaves the leakage untouched. Course III is appropriate because it measures the leakage so that repairs can be prioritised and their effect verified. Therefore, courses I and III should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Storm-water drains in a locality are choked with silt and plastic just before the monsoon.

Courses of Action:
I. Wait for the first heavy rain to check whether the drains overflow before deciding on cleaning.
II. Desilt and clean the drains before the rains and prepare a schedule for pre-monsoon cleaning every year.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.

questions.explanationText: Course II prevents the flooding that choked drains would cause. Course I allows a predictable problem to occur before any action is taken. Therefore, only course II is justified.

questions.questionText:
A bus shelter on a highway is used by about two hundred passengers daily but has no roof in the rainy season.

Courses of Action:
I. Ask passengers to wait inside the nearby shop until the bus arrives.
II. Construct a shelter at the stop and review whether other high-use stops in the district need the same facility.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course II provides the missing facility and plans for similar points. Course I depends on the goodwill of a private shop and leaves the passengers exposed. Therefore, course II is the better course of action.

questions.questionText:
An unmanned railway level crossing in a district is used by school children twice a day.

Courses of Action:
I. Arrange an awareness and safety programme and press the railway authority for gates, a gatekeeper or a diversion.
II. Approach the railway authority to install gates or a gatekeeper and, until then, arrange trained volunteers and warning signs at the crossing.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I only explains the danger and leaves the crossing as it is. Course II pursues a permanent safeguard as well as interim protection for the children who cross daily. Therefore, only course II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Pedestrians cross a highway at a busy point because the nearest footbridge is 700 metres away.

Courses of Action:
I. Erect a fence along the median and ask pedestrians to use the existing footbridge.
II. Construct a footbridge or underpass at the point of maximum crossing and, until it is ready, install a signal-controlled crossing.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both courses should be implemented.
Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course II removes the reason people cross at a dangerous point. Course I pushes pedestrians to a long detour that they will simply ignore, which is why they cross there already. Therefore, course II should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
Vehicles are parked in every available space around a market area, blocking the movement of pedestrians and emergency vehicles.

Courses of Action:
I. Widen the road by removing the footpath so that the parked vehicles occupy the space that is freed.
II. Allow parking anywhere but charge a small fee to discourage it.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I takes space away from pedestrians for parking and would push them onto the carriageway without solving the parking problem. Course II accepts the obstruction and only adds a charge that will not free the road. Therefore, neither course is justified.

questions.questionText:
Ambulances are delayed during peak hours on a busy city corridor.

Courses of Action:
I. Ask ambulances to use the outer ring road whatever the distance.
II. Notify hospitals to advise emergency callers, and coordinate with traffic police to clear the corridor for approaching ambulances.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course II reduces the delay on the route where it occurs and keeps the pre-hospital information flowing. Course I adds avoidable travel distance and would delay critical cases further. Therefore, course II is the better course of action.

questions.questionText:
Residents of an apartment complex face frequent power interruptions, and lifts and water pumps stop working each time.

Courses of Action:
I. Take up the outage pattern with the electricity utility and install an inverter-backed supply for the lifts and pumps.
II. Ask residents to use the stairs and store water in buckets for such periods.
III. Shift the pumps' operating hours to the part of the day when the supply is more reliable.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course III should be followed.
Courses I and III should be followed.
None of the courses should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I pursues the supply problem and protects essential services in the meantime. Course II shifts the burden to residents, including the elderly and those who cannot use the stairs. Course III is appropriate because it uses the hours of reliable supply and reduces the effect of the interruptions on essential services. Therefore, courses I and III should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Buses on a city route run irregularly and often arrive three or four at the same time.

Courses of Action:
I. Add more buses to the route without changing how departures are managed.
II. Review the timetable and the boarding time at stops, and introduce position tracking so that departures are spaced properly.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course II corrects the bunching problem by managing departures. Course I adds capacity without removing the cause of the irregular running, which would leave the same pattern. Therefore, only course II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A truck has broken down in the middle lane of a busy flyover during the morning rush.

Courses of Action:
I. Wait for the truck's owner to arrange a mechanic.
II. Alert the traffic control room, place warning triangles, and arrange a towing vehicle through the standard emergency procedure.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course II protects other road users and restores traffic through the proper mechanism. Course I leaves a live hazard in a traffic lane for an indefinite period. Therefore, course II should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
Footpaths on the main road are broken and uneven, and pedestrians walk on the carriageway instead.

Courses of Action:
I. Close the broken pavements for pedestrians permanently and remove them.
II. Repair and level the pavements in phases and remove the obstructions placed on them.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I takes away the pedestrian facility altogether. Course II restores the facility that pedestrians are supposed to use and deals with the obstructions that discourage them. Therefore, only course II is justified.

questions.questionText:
Street vendors occupy a large part of the road outside a market and traffic slows to a crawl.

Courses of Action:
I. Allow the vendors to remain in place but ask them to keep their wares as far to the side as possible.
II. Evict the vendors without providing any alternative place to sell.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I depends on the vendors' restraint and leaves the carriageway obstructed, so traffic would continue to slow near the market. Course II merely moves the congestion to another street and creates a fresh social problem. Therefore, neither is a reasonable course of action.

questions.questionText:
Water supplied by tankers to a housing colony looks muddy and some residents have fallen ill.

Courses of Action:
I. Advise residents to drink the water only after adding purification tablets they buy themselves.
II. Stop the supply from that source, get the water tested and arrange supply from a verified source.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course II removes the unsafe source and establishes whether it is contaminated. Course I transfers the responsibility for a public supply failure to individual residents and leaves the source in use. Therefore, only course II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Garbage in a locality is collected irregularly and waste is dumped on a vacant plot.

Courses of Action:
I. Fix a published collection schedule, clear the accumulated waste and fence the plot until it is developed.
II. Post a notice warning residents against dumping waste.
III. Impose a fine on any household whose waste is found on the street.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course II should be followed.
Courses I and II should be followed.
All three courses should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I removes the cause of the dumping by restoring regular collection. Course II issues an instruction while the collection failure continues. Course III imposes a penalty before a dependable collection service exists, which punishes residents for a failure of the service itself. Therefore, only course I should be followed.

questions.questionText:
An open dumping ground beside a government school attracts flies and stray animals.

Courses of Action:
I. Ask the school to keep its windows closed during class hours.
II. Cover and relocate the dumping activity, clean the site and arrange daily collection at a proper facility.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course II removes the health risk from the school's surroundings. Course I leaves the cause in place and transfers the difficulty to children in classrooms. Therefore, course II should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
A river passing a town has developed thick foam and a foul smell over the last month.

Courses of Action:
I. Advise residents to stay away from the river until the foam disappears naturally.
II. Trace the sources of discharge along the stretch, direct the polluters to stop it and monitor the water quality regularly.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course II identifies the polluters and creates continuing oversight. Course I accepts pollution as a temporary inconvenience instead of an offence to be stopped. Therefore, only course II is justified.

questions.questionText:
Residents living near an industrial estate complain of smoke and a strong smell at night.

Courses of Action:
I. Ask the units to operate only during the day so that the smell appears at other times.
II. Inspect the units' emission controls, act against those exceeding limits and install continuous air-quality monitoring in the area.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course II addresses the emissions themselves and gives the community evidence of improvement. Course I merely shifts the nuisance to different hours. Therefore, course II is the better course of action.

questions.questionText:
The groundwater level in a town has fallen sharply and borewells are being drilled deeper every year.

Courses of Action:
I. Depend on water brought by tankers from distant sources.
II. Make rainwater harvesting mandatory for new buildings, recharge existing wells and regulate the extraction of groundwater.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course II rebuilds the resource that is being depleted. Course I treats the shortage as a transport problem and leaves the aquifer to fall further. Therefore, only course II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Plastic bottles and bags have accumulated in a lake used for festivals and drinking water.

Courses of Action:
I. Fence the lake and prevent the public from approaching it.
II. Organise a phased clean-up with the local body, place waste bins around the lake and enforce a ban on single-use plastic in the area.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.
Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course II removes the waste and reduces the flow of new litter. Course I denies a community its water body without cleaning it. Therefore, course II should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
A hill road is losing soil from the slope after heavy rain, and rocks fall on the carriageway.

Courses of Action:
I. Leave the slope as it is and rely on vehicles to avoid falling rocks.
II. Restrict traffic during heavy rain, clear the debris immediately and take up bio-engineering of the slope with proper drainage.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.

questions.explanationText: Course II protects road users now and stabilises the slope for the long term. Course I leaves a known hazard unmanaged and places the risk on the travelling public. Therefore, only course II is justified.

questions.questionText:
Air quality near a busy junction in a city has been recorded as poor on most days.

Courses of Action:
I. Shift the entire traffic of the junction to residential streets to spread the pollution.
II. Improve traffic flow through signal coordination, promote tree plantation along the roads and monitor pollution regularly.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course II reduces emissions at the source and tracks the change. Course I relocates the pollution into areas where people live and does not reduce the total emissions. Therefore, course II is the better course of action.

questions.questionText:
A chemical unit is discharging coloured effluent into a canal used by farmers for irrigation.

Courses of Action:
I. Ask the farmers to irrigate only in the evening when the colour is not visible.
II. Sample the effluent, issue directions for treatment before discharge and require the unit to upgrade its effluent plant.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course II stops the pollution at its source. Course I accepts contaminated water for food crops and does not address the discharge. Therefore, only course II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Loudspeakers from a commercial complex continue late into the night near a hospital zone.

Courses of Action:
I. Ask the hospital to shift its patients to the side away from the road.
II. Enforce the silence-zone rules through the authorities, fix responsibilities on the commercial establishment and display the noise limits.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.
Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.
