questions.explanationText: Course II applies the existing rule to the source of the noise. Course I transfers the difficulty to patients instead of enforcing the rule that exists. Therefore, course II should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
Trees on a roadside have been felled for a commercial construction and no replacement has been made.

Courses of Action:
I. Ignore the felling since the building work already supports employment.
II. Verify whether the required permissions were obtained, and require compensatory planting to a prescribed standard.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course II checks compliance and restores the environmental loss. Course I treats an unrelated benefit as a reason to overlook a possible violation. Therefore, only course II is justified.

questions.questionText:
A fire has broken out in a large landfill and thick smoke is spreading towards houses.

Courses of Action:
I. Allow the fire to burn out on its own to avoid disturbing the waste.
II. Inform the fire and pollution authorities, cordon the area and manage the gas and smoke by covering the burning waste with inert material.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course II brings trained resources and reduces the smoke hazard for residents. Course I leaves a fire to spread gases and smoke across a populated area. Therefore, course II is the better course of action.

questions.questionText:
Farmers in a district burn crop residue every winter and the smoke affects a nearby town.

Courses of Action:
I. Prohibit burning and prosecute farmers who use the practice without giving them any alternative.
II. Provide information on alternative residue management and support machinery for it, with monitoring during the season.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course II offers a workable alternative to the practice that causes the smoke. Course I imposes a penalty on farmers who have no other means of clearing the residue and would be difficult to implement. Therefore, only course II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A village's drinking water source has shown bacterial contamination in a routine test.

Courses of Action:
I. Ask residents to boil water and continue using the same source until the next test.
II. Stop the source from being used, supply safe water and treat or disinfect the source before it is put back into service.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.
Neither course should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course II removes the contamination and restores a safe supply. Course I leaves a known contaminated source in use and depends on every household taking precautions every day. Therefore, course II should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
Several people fell ill after attending a community feast organised by a local body.

Courses of Action:
I. Announce that the illness was caused by the weather and close the matter.
II. Report the matter to the health authority, get the food samples and water tested and stop any leftover food from being consumed.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course II establishes the cause and prevents further cases. Course I suppresses the enquiry that would identify the contaminated food or water. Therefore, only course II is justified.

questions.questionText:
Workers near a furnace in a plant have complained of dizziness and exhaustion during their shifts.

Courses of Action:
I. Rotate the workers every hour without changing the conditions near the furnace.
II. Provide immediate first aid, review the ventilation and work-rest cycles of the area and arrange a medical assessment by the plant's medical officer.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.

questions.explanationText: Course II treats the immediate symptoms and corrects the working conditions that cause them. Course I moves the same hazard to other workers without reducing the heat stress. Therefore, course II is the better course of action.

questions.questionText:
A fire exit of a shopping complex is blocked by cartons and old furniture.

Courses of Action:
I. Ask the security staff to check the exit at the end of every day.
II. Keep the goods there but ask staff to move them quickly if a fire occurs.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I introduces a routine check that still leaves the exit blocked for the rest of the day, when the risk is just as real. Course II depends on a reaction that nobody can guarantee during an actual fire. Therefore, neither course should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A factory has no documented emergency response plan even though it stores flammable material.

Courses of Action:
I. Keep the material in a locked store and hope that no incident occurs.
II. Prepare a written emergency plan, train the workers and test it with periodic evacuation drills.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course II prepares the organisation for an event that its own material makes possible. Course I does nothing to reduce the risk or prepare the workforce. Therefore, course II should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
Stagnant water collects in discarded containers in a locality and mosquito-borne illness has increased.

Courses of Action:
I. Advise residents to sleep under nets without removing the breeding sites.
II. Remove the stagnant water and containers, carry out a fogging and awareness drive and repeat the checks through the season.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course II eliminates the breeding grounds that produce the mosquitoes. Course I helps individuals at night while the source of the problem continues to multiply. Therefore, only course II is justified.

questions.questionText:
A road-cutting contractor has left an open trench at a busy corner without any warning sign.

Courses of Action:
I. Ask pedestrians to be careful while crossing near the trench.
II. Inform the civic authority at once, place barricades and warning boards, and require the contractor to restore the surface.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course II removes a hazard that has a clear responsible party. Course I places the risk of an unsafe work site on the public. Therefore, course II is the better course of action.

questions.questionText:
Chemicals in a college laboratory are stored without labels and incompatibles are kept on the same shelf.

Courses of Action:
I. Label all the containers and segregate them according to the safety data sheets.
II. Move all the chemicals to a locked room under a single key holder.
III. Ask the laboratory staff to learn the storage rules from a training programme.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Courses II and III should be followed.
All three courses should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Courses I and II should be followed.

questions.explanationText: All three courses are practical and complementary: labelling identifies the contents, segregation prevents dangerous reactions and training enables staff to apply the rules correctly. Each is feasible in a laboratory of this kind, so all three should be followed. Therefore, all three courses should be followed.

questions.questionText:
School children in a rural area do not wash their hands before the mid-day meal.

Courses of Action:
I. Ask the children's families to ensure hygiene at home and take no action at school.
II. Provide water, soap and hand-washing stations at the school, and include hand hygiene in the daily routine with the teachers' supervision.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course II makes the practice possible and routine where the meal is served. Course I looks elsewhere for a problem that can be corrected at the school itself. Therefore, only course II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Food handlers in a market area have not undergone the required periodic health checks for years.

Courses of Action:
I. Arrange health checks for the handlers through the health authority and make the certificate a condition for continuing their work.
II. Arrange the health checks through the health authority at the market itself on fixed days.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.
Neither course should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I applies the existing public-health requirement to those who handle food. Course II is appropriate because it makes the requirement easy to meet instead of only insisting on it. Therefore, both courses should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
A cinema hall keeps its emergency exit doors locked to prevent ticketless entry.

Courses of Action:
I. Permit the doors to remain locked but ask staff to unlock them if a fire is noticed.
II. Require the doors to be kept openable from inside with an alarm-linked latch and have the arrangement inspected regularly.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course II keeps the exit usable in an emergency while addressing the concern about entry. Course I relies on human reaction during a fire, when exits must open by themselves. Therefore, only course II is justified.

questions.questionText:
A public toilet near a bus stand is unusable because of poor maintenance.

Courses of Action:
I. Keep the toilet shut so that its condition does not deteriorate further.
II. Award a maintenance contract with a service standard, inspect it periodically and provide water supply to the facility.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course II restores and sustains an essential public facility. Course I withdraws a service that travellers need and leaves the built asset unused. Therefore, course II is the better course of action.

questions.questionText:
The railing of a footbridge over a canal is broken at several places.

Courses of Action:
I. Ask users to cross the bridge without leaning on the railing.
II. Cordon the broken sections, place warning boards and take up repair work on priority.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course II prevents a fall and restores a safe passage. Course I places the safety of the structure on the caution of the people using it. Therefore, only course II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Copper cables have been stolen from streetlight poles in a district three times in a year.

Courses of Action:
I. Stop using those streetlights so that there is nothing left to steal.
II. Coordinate with the police for patrolling and surveillance in the affected stretches, and consider theft-resistant fittings for future work.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.
Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course II protects public property while keeping the service. Course I leaves an entire stretch dark, which invites other crimes. Therefore, course II should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
A bus route used by factory workers has no service after seven in the evening.

Courses of Action:
I. Ask the factories to alter their shift timings to match the available buses.
II. Assess the demand with the industries along the route and arrange additional evening trips accordingly.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course II matches the service to the demonstrated need of the workers. Course I asks industry to reorganise production around a transport limitation instead of correcting it. Therefore, only course II is justified.

questions.questionText:
An underpass in a city gets waterlogged even after moderate rain.

Courses of Action:
I. Clear the drains and pumping arrangement, pump out the water during rain and review the drainage design of the underpass.
II. Barricade the underpass for the whole of the rainy season.
III. Station a pump at the underpass throughout the monsoon until the drainage is redesigned.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: None of the courses should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course III should be followed.
Courses I and III should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I manages the flooding in the short term and corrects the design that causes it. Course II removes an important route for the season instead of solving a manageable problem. Course III is appropriate as a temporary measure that keeps the underpass usable while the drainage is redesigned. Therefore, courses I and III should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Several manhole covers are missing on a city road and some are below the road level.

Courses of Action:
I. Mark the open manholes with chalk so that road users can see them.
II. Advise motorists to drive slowly along that road.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I provides a faint marking that will not survive traffic or rain and leaves an open hole in the carriageway. Course II depends on caution to avoid an open hole that should not exist at all. Therefore, neither is a reasonable course of action.

questions.questionText:
Unauthorised constructions have come up on a footpath, forcing pedestrians onto the road.

Courses of Action:
I. Verify the legality of the structures, direct their removal under the existing rules and restore the footpath.
II. Widen the carriageway so that pedestrians can walk on a part of it.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I restores the public space that belongs to pedestrians. Course II gives more space to vehicles and legitimises the loss of the footpath. Therefore, only course I should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Stray dogs have become aggressive in a locality where garbage is dumped in the open.

Courses of Action:
I. Coordinate with the animal husbandry or municipal authority for sterilisation and vaccination, and remove the open garbage that feeds the animals.
II. Drive the dogs out towards the neighbouring locality.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both courses should be implemented.
Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I uses the proper authority and removes the food source that sustains the population. Course II merely moves the problem into someone else's area. Therefore, course I should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
A streetlight pole in a market area is leaning dangerously after a storm.

Courses of Action:
I. Warn shopkeepers and the public, rope off the area and have the pole secured or replaced by the electrical authority.
II. Ask people to avoid standing near the pole until someone reports it.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I creates a safe zone and puts the repair in motion. Course II leaves a live hazard in a crowded place and transfers the responsibility to the public. Therefore, only course I is justified.

questions.questionText:
The play equipment in a public park is broken and children continue to climb on it.

Courses of Action:
I. Barricade the equipment, place a notice and repair or replace the damaged parts before reopening the area.
II. Remove the play equipment from the park altogether.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I removes the risk and restores the facility. Course II permanently takes away a recreation facility that the neighbourhood's children use. Therefore, course I is the better course of action.

questions.questionText:
The overhead water tank of a housing society has not been cleaned for three years.

Courses of Action:
I. Schedule the tank cleaning, test the water afterwards and record the cleaning dates for future reference.
II. Add more chlorine to the water so that cleaning becomes unnecessary.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I removes the sediment and contamination that cleaning is meant to address. Course II tries to treat the water without finding out what is at the bottom of the tank. Therefore, only course I should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A storm-water drain has been covered by an illegal structure that diverts water into nearby homes.

Courses of Action:
I. Direct the removal of the structure under the existing rules and restore the drain to its original width.
II. Raise the height of the nearby homes' thresholds so that water does not enter.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.
Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I removes the obstruction that causes the flooding. Course II treats each home separately and leaves a public drain blocked. Therefore, course I should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
Music from a marriage hall plays loudly past midnight, and residents nearby cannot sleep.

Courses of Action:
I. Ask the organisers to observe the permitted hours and levels, and inform the authority for action if the practice continues.
II. Ban all functions in the hall permanently.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I enforces the existing limits proportionately. Course II removes a legitimate community facility because of a rule violation that can be corrected. Therefore, only course I is justified.

questions.questionText:
A locality has faced a serious water shortage for two weeks because a supply line has failed.

Courses of Action:
I. Advise residents to store water whenever it is available and to wait until the line is repaired.
II. Suspend supply to the whole city for two days so that the line can be repaired.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I asks the residents to manage without supply and puts no repair plan in place. Course II spreads the pain of an equipment failure to users who are not affected at all. Therefore, neither is a reasonable course of action.

questions.questionText:
Water in a town is supplied only on alternate days, and residents want a daily supply.

Courses of Action:
I. Publish the supply schedule clearly and monitor the pressure to ensure that the available water reaches the ends of the network.
II. Increase the water charges heavily so that residents use less and the supply lasts longer.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I improves the reliability of what the residents already receive. Course II raises the cost without improving the service or adding a drop of water. Therefore, only course I should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A city junction records traffic jams during the evening peak although the road is wide.

Courses of Action:
I. Re-time the signals using traffic counts, restrict on-street parking near the junction and deploy traffic wardens at the peak.
II. Raise the speed limit so that vehicles clear the junction faster.
III. Widen the road at the junction by removing the footpath.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: None of the courses should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Courses II and III should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I removes the causes of the queueing at the junction. Course II is not related to the obstruction that slows traffic and would make the junction less safe. Course III solves the congestion by taking space away from pedestrians and would push them onto the carriageway. Therefore, only course I should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A footbridge is being used by vendors and parked vehicles, blocking movement for pedestrians.

Courses of Action:
I. Clear the footbridge of trading and parking with warning notices, provide a nearby vending zone and enforce the rules.
II. Build a second footbridge immediately without changing how the first one is used.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both courses should be implemented.
Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I recovers the existing pedestrian facility and offers an alternative for the vendors. Course II spends heavily without dealing with the misuse that would repeat itself. Therefore, course I should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
Residents complain that garbage is being burnt in the open by the collection staff.

Courses of Action:
I. Instruct the collection staff to stop the practice, provide proper collection and disposal routes and arrange supervision.
II. Ask residents to keep their waste wet so that it does not catch fire.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I corrects the disposal practice that causes the smoke. Course II asks residents to manage the consequence of a wrong practice by the staff. Therefore, only course I is justified.

questions.questionText:
Two-wheelers are parked on the ramp meant for wheelchairs at a public building.

Courses of Action:
I. Mark the ramp clearly, place deterrent signage and arrange alternative parking for two-wheelers nearby.
II. Remove the ramp because it is being misused.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I protects an accessibility facility that a particular group of users needs. Course II removes the facility for the users it was built for, because others misuse it. Therefore, course I is the better course of action.

questions.questionText:
A district hospital's ambulance is often stuck in traffic because drivers do not make way.

Courses of Action:
I. Run a public awareness campaign about giving way to ambulances and coordinate with traffic police for enforcement.
II. Advise the hospital to schedule ambulance trips only at night.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I addresses the behaviour and enforcement gap that delays the ambulance. Course II leaves emergency patients without timely transport because of a problem that can be corrected. Therefore, only course I should be followed.

questions.questionText:
An open well in a village is used for drinking water and is also used for washing clothes and bathing animals.

Courses of Action:
I. Separate the uses by providing a bathing and washing area elsewhere and protect the well with a parapet and a drain.
II. Ask the residents to draw only the water they need for drinking.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I removes the contamination risk from the practice itself. Course II depends on individual restraint while the same well continues to serve incompatible uses. Therefore, course I should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
A stretch of a highway has no safe pedestrian crossing although a school and a bus stop are on either side.

Courses of Action:
I. Provide a zebra crossing with signage and a signal or refuge island, and ask the school to arrange supervised crossing.
II. Advise the school children to walk to the nearest town to cross the road.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I creates a safe crossing where the demand is concentrated. Course II sends children on a long walk on the same unsafe road. Therefore, only course I is justified.

questions.questionText:
The municipal waste collection vehicle arrives at unpredictable hours, and residents miss it and dump waste on the street.

Courses of Action:
I. Ask the residents to deposit their waste at the ward office instead.
II. Ask residents to keep their waste at home until the vehicle arrives.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I shifts the collecting duty to the residents rather than making the collection service predictable. Course II is not practical for households that must store waste for an unknown period. Therefore, neither is a reasonable course of action.

questions.questionText:
A flyover in a city has exposed reinforcement on its pillars and the concrete has started to flake.

Courses of Action:
I. Restrict the heaviest vehicles, arrange a structural assessment and begin repair work as per the assessment.
II. Paint the pillars so that the damage is not visible to the public.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I deals with a structural concern in the proper sequence of assessment and repair. Course II hides the symptom of a defect that could develop into a failure. Therefore, only course I should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Illegal tapping of electricity from streetlight poles has been reported in a slum area.

Courses of Action:
I. Inspect the connections, regularise the supply through metered connections where possible and remove the unsafe tapping with the utility's help.
II. Remove all streetlight poles from the area so that tapping becomes impossible.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I corrects an unsafe practice and moves the users to a legal supply. Course II takes away lighting from the whole area and would create a safety problem at night. Therefore, course I should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
A public park has become a place for anti-social activity after dark because it has no lighting or gates.

Courses of Action:
I. Install lighting, arrange for the park to be opened and closed at fixed hours and involve a residents' committee in its upkeep.
II. Close the park permanently to all visitors.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I makes the park usable and supervised during defined hours. Course II withdraws a public facility instead of managing it. Therefore, only course I is justified.

questions.questionText:
A temple town's narrow lanes are choked by tourist vehicles during the festival season.

Courses of Action:
I. Operate shuttle services from peripheral parking lots, restrict private vehicles in the core area during the festival and publish the arrangements in advance.
II. Ban visitors from entering the town during the festival.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I manages the peak in a way that keeps the town open to visitors. Course II destroys the event and the town's income instead of planning for the crowd. Therefore, course I is the better course of action.

questions.questionText:
A state transport bus stand has no separate area for women and the elderly to wait.

Courses of Action:
I. Provide a covered waiting area with seating and toilets for women, the elderly and those with children.
II. Ask the bus crew to give priority boarding without any separate facility.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I adds a facility proportionate to the need it identifies. Course II is a well-meant instruction that does not provide the space or comfort that is missing. Therefore, only course I should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A newly paved road has developed cracks within three months of completion.

Courses of Action:
I. Inspect the work against the specification, hold the contractor responsible under the defect-liability clause and have the stretch re-laid.
II. Resurface the road again out of the municipality's own funds without examining the cause.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.
Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I fixes the responsibility and checks the quality of the original work. Course II pays a second time for a defect that the contract already covers. Therefore, course I should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
Several customers of a bank have reported unauthorised transactions on their debit cards within a week of using a particular ATM.

Courses of Action:
I. Block the reported cards, refund the disputed amounts after verification and inspect that ATM for skimming or tampering.
II. Ask the customers to change their personal identification numbers and wait for more complaints.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I protects the affected customers and checks the equipment that is suspected. Course II leaves both the customers and the suspected machine in the same condition. Therefore, only course I is justified.

questions.questionText:
The system flags a series of large transactions from an account that usually sees only small transfers.

Courses of Action:
I. Block the account permanently so that no wrong transaction can take place.
II. Allow the transactions to proceed and review the account at the end of the month.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I blocks a legitimate customer's account without any verification, which would harm an account holder who has done nothing wrong. Course II allows an unusual pattern to complete and reviews it only much later. Therefore, neither is a reasonable course of action.

questions.questionText:
An ATM in a busy market area runs out of cash every weekend and customers return without money.

Courses of Action:
I. Review the withdrawal data for weekends, increase the cash loading for that machine and monitor the refill schedule.
II. Ask customers to use other ATMs that are located further away.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I matches the cash replenishment to the demand the machine actually faces. Course II leaves the machine unusable at the hours when it is needed most. Therefore, only course I should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A customer's account has been debited twice for a single online payment.

Courses of Action:
I. Verify the duplicate entry with the payment records, reverse the extra debit and inform the customer of the correction.
II. Ask the customer to raise the issue with the merchant and close the matter.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.
Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I corrects an error made in the bank's own records. Course II transfers a reconciliation duty to the customer, who has no access to the bank's systems. Therefore, course I should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
A branch's loan defaults have risen sharply in one product category.

Courses of Action:
I. Analyse the default cases for weaknesses in appraisal and monitoring and tighten the process for that product.
II. Stop lending altogether in that branch until the defaults fall.
III. Introduce a reminder and follow-up routine for accounts that miss an instalment.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Courses I and III should be followed.
All three courses should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Courses I and II should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I corrects whatever is wrong in the appraisal process. Course II shuts down legitimate lending for all customers of the branch, which is far wider than the problem. Course III is appropriate because follow-up at the first missed instalment prevents an account from drifting into default. Therefore, courses I and III should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A caller claims to be from the bank's technical team and asks customers for their one-time passwords.

Courses of Action:
I. Warn customers through messages and branch notices, train staff to recognise such calls and register complaints with the police.
II. Change the bank's helpline number so that customers do not get confused.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I addresses the fraud attempt through awareness and reporting. Course II changes something unrelated to the callers who are making the attempts. Therefore, only course I is justified.

questions.questionText:
Several cheques presented at a branch have been returned because of differences in the signature by the same customer.

Courses of Action:
I. Contact the customer, verify the signature afresh against the bank's records and update the specimen with proper authorisation.
II. Return every cheque from that customer without explanation.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I resolves the mismatch fairly through the established verification process. Course II refuses service without giving the customer a chance to correct the record. Therefore, course I is the better course of action.

questions.questionText:
The bank's mobile payment application fails during festival shopping hours when volumes are highest.

Courses of Action:
I. Reduce the maximum payment amount allowed during festivals so that fewer transactions fail.
II. Request customers to make payments through the branch counters during festivals.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I limits what customers may spend at the busiest time instead of preparing the system for the demand. Course II pushes customers to a slower channel at the busiest time. Therefore, neither course should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Customers have lost money after using unauthorised lending applications advertised on social media.

Courses of Action:
I. Issue advisories listing the bank's official applications, help affected customers report the matter and coordinate with authorities against the fake applications.
II. Ask the customers to recover the money from the application's owners themselves.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.
Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I protects customers and channels the complaint to where action is possible. Course II leaves customers to pursue unidentified operators on their own. Therefore, course I should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
Customers stand in long queues at a branch every month for pension related work.

Courses of Action:
I. Ask the pensioners' associations to collect the payments on behalf of their members.
II. Advise pensioners to visit the branch on less crowded days.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I makes an informal body responsible for individual payments and creates a fresh risk to money that must reach each pensioner directly. Course II depends on the convenience of the customers rather than on any change by the bank. Therefore, neither course is justified.

questions.questionText:
Pension payments in a district are delayed every month because the records are verified by hand.

Courses of Action:
I. Digitise the beneficiary records with bank-account-based transfers and publish a payment date for each month.
II. Ask pensioners to collect their payments from the district office in person.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I removes the manual verification that causes the delay. Course II adds a further burden on the beneficiaries for the same payment. Therefore, course I is the better course of action.

questions.questionText:
A government ration shop has been accused of issuing less than the entitled quantity.

Courses of Action:
I. Inspect the shop's stock and weighing records, verify the distribution register and act against the dealer if the shortfall is established.
II. Close all the ration shops of the district until the enquiry is complete.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I verifies the specific complaint with records and takes proportionate action. Course II punishes the entire district for an allegation against one shop. Therefore, only course I should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Obtaining a birth certificate in a town requires four visits to different offices.

Courses of Action:
I. Map the steps, merge them into a single application with digital verification and publish a service standard for delivery.
II. Ask applicants to appoint a local agent to complete the process for them.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.
Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I removes the procedural burden that causes repeated visits. Course II institutionalises the inconvenience and adds a cost for the applicant. Therefore, course I should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
The public grievance portal has more than half of its complaints pending beyond the prescribed period.

Courses of Action:
I. Publish the pending cases by department with reasons, and fix accountability for disposal within the prescribed timeline.
II. Stop accepting new complaints until the pending ones are cleared.
III. Hold a monthly review with the department heads on the disposal of pending complaints.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course III should be followed.
Courses I and III should be followed.
None of the courses should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I acts on the backlog with transparency and responsibility. Course II blocks the channel that citizens are using, which would hide rather than solve the problem. Course III is appropriate because a regular review keeps the backlog under attention until it is cleared. Therefore, courses I and III should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Meals served in a government school are reported to be of poor quality and quantity.

Courses of Action:
I. Constitute a monitoring committee with parents and teachers, and inspect the kitchen and the supplied provisions regularly.
II. Ask the students to bring food from home instead.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I creates an accountable check on the quality being questioned. Course II shifts the responsibility to families for a service that the school is supposed to provide. Therefore, only course I is justified.

questions.questionText:
Patients at a government hospital wait for hours for routine consultations because of a lack of doctors at certain times.

Courses of Action:
I. Raise the consultation fee during the busiest hours so that fewer patients come at those times.
II. Ask patients to come only during the hours when fewer people are present.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I reduces the crowd by making treatment costlier at the hours when working people can attend, which is neither fair nor effective. Course II leaves the staffing imbalance unaddressed. Therefore, neither is a reasonable course of action.

questions.questionText:
An application for a fire-safety certificate needs clearance from three offices but there is no way to track it.

Courses of Action:
I. Introduce a single-window application with an online status tracker and defined timelines for each clearance.
II. Reduce the validity of the certificate to six months so that the process is repeated more often.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I simplifies a process whose complexity causes the delay. Course II increases the frequency of the very process that is the problem. Therefore, only course I should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Farmers in a district have found errors in their land records.

Courses of Action:
I. Order a fresh survey of all the land in the district before any correction is made.
II. Freeze all land transactions of the district until every record is checked.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.
Neither course should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I delays every correction until an entire district has been surveyed, which is far beyond what the reported errors require. Course II paralyses all land transactions for a problem that affects a limited number of records. Therefore, neither course should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
Stray cattle wandering on a state highway have caused two accidents this month.

Courses of Action:
I. Coordinate with the municipal and animal husbandry authorities to shift the animals to a shelter and stop the roadside feeding and dumping that attracts them.
II. Ask drivers to reduce their speed on that stretch of highway.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I removes the animals from the carriageway and the cause that brings them there. Course II places the safety burden on road users while the hazard continues. Therefore, only course I is justified.

questions.questionText:
A community hall rented out for functions has poor hygiene and no staff on duty.

Courses of Action:
I. Provide a maintenance contract with a cleaning schedule, keep a caretaker on duty and publish the booking conditions.
II. Sub-let the hall to a private operator without any conditions.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I fixes the upkeep of a public asset with defined responsibility. Course II hands over a facility without setting any standard for it. Therefore, course I is the better course of action.

questions.questionText:
A local committee has received many complaints about loud music playing beyond the permitted hours during festivals.

Courses of Action:
I. Notify the organisers of the permitted levels and hours in advance, and monitor the main sites with the police where needed.
II. Cancel all festival celebrations in the locality.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I encourages compliance with the existing rules and monitors the sites where violations are likely. Course II cancels the celebrations for everyone because of a few organisers. Therefore, only course I should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Benches, lights and plants in a public park have been damaged repeatedly by vandals.

Courses of Action:
I. Repair the damage, add lighting and involve a residents' group in the upkeep to build local ownership.
II. Erect a high wall around the park and keep it locked.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I restores the park and adds the supervision that deters damage. Course II converts a public park into a closed structure that the neighbourhood cannot use. Therefore, course I should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
Many books in a public library are missing and members are unable to borrow the titles they want.

Courses of Action:
I. Ask the members to donate a book each year to replace the missing titles.
II. Take a large deposit from every member and reduce the lending period to one week.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I asks the members to replace stock that the library has lost, which does not recover the missing books or prevent further loss. Course II burdens all members with a costly deposit for the losses of a few. Therefore, neither course is justified.

questions.questionText:
A neighbourhood has seen a rise in burglaries at night.

Courses of Action:
I. Coordinate a neighbourhood watch with the police station, improve lighting in the lanes and report suspicious activity through a common channel.
II. Advise residents to keep their valuables in a bank locker and take no other step.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I reduces the opportunity for burglary through community and physical measures. Course II accepts the crime as routine and does not engage with prevention. Therefore, course I is the better course of action.

questions.questionText:
A state scholarship scheme for students has very few applicants even though thousands are eligible.

Courses of Action:
I. Simplify the application, publicise the scheme through schools and colleges and hold camps to help students apply.
II. Reduce the number of scholarships on offer to match the number of applicants.
III. Increase the value of each scholarship to attract more applicants.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Courses II and III should be followed.
All three courses should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Courses I and II should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I increases awareness and removes the difficulty in applying. Course II reduces a benefit that students are entitled to because it has not been communicated. Course III spends more money without addressing the reason eligible students are not applying for the scheme at all. Therefore, only course I should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A blood donation camp in a college collected far fewer units than expected.

Courses of Action:
I. Publicise the camp in advance, coordinate with voluntary organisations and make it convenient for donors by fixing timings and a location near hostels.
II. Make donations compulsory for the students of one department.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I addresses the reasons for the low turnout with mobilisation and convenience. Course II produces unwilling donors and defeats the purpose of voluntary donation. Therefore, only course I should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A community water tank in a locality leaks continuously and the locality faces a shortage in summer.

Courses of Action:
I. Ask the residents to fetch water from the neighbouring locality until the tank is repaired.
II. Reduce the supply hours to the locality so that less water is wasted.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both courses should be implemented.
Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I makes the locality depend on its neighbours for an indefinite period instead of repairing its own tank. Course II increases the scarcity that residents are already facing. Therefore, neither course should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
Pedestrians outside a school gate are at risk because vehicles use the road at high speed during the morning hours.

Courses of Action:
I. Install a speed-calming measure and a signalled crossing at the school gate, and coordinate with the traffic police for enforcement during school hours.
II. Ask the school to start its sessions earlier so that the crowd disperses before the traffic builds up.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I creates a safe environment at the point where the risk is greatest. Course II shifts the school's routine while the road remains as dangerous as before. Therefore, only course I is justified.

questions.questionText:
A municipal market has been built with old wiring, and shopkeepers use additional appliances beyond the permitted load.

Courses of Action:
I. Get the wiring inspected and upgraded, cap the load per shop with metered limits and conduct periodic safety checks.
II. Ask shopkeepers to use only one appliance at a time without changing the wiring.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I removes the electrical hazard that the older wiring creates. Course II places the risk on voluntary restraint and leaves the wiring untouched. Therefore, course I is the better course of action.

questions.questionText:
An emergency ward is crowded and patients with minor ailments are occupying beds needed by serious cases.

Courses of Action:
I. Introduce triage so that minor cases are diverted to the outpatient or primary-care facility.
II. Increase the number of beds in the ward without changing the way patients are admitted.
III. Close the emergency ward and refer every case to a larger hospital in another city.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Courses I and III should be followed.
All three courses should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Courses I and II should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Courses I and II improve the capacity of the ward to treat serious cases: triage frees beds for those who need them, and additional beds raise the capacity for genuine emergencies. Course III removes emergency care from the area altogether, which would put lives at risk. Therefore, courses I and II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A district receives a cyclone warning three days in advance of landfall.

Courses of Action:
I. Move people from low-lying areas to identified shelters and stock supplies at the shelters.
II. Suspend fishing, transport and construction activity in the coastal belt for the warned period.
III. Wait for the cyclone to make landfall before taking any district-wide step.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Courses II and III should be followed.
Courses I and II should be followed.
None of the courses should be followed.
Only course III should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Courses I and II are the standard preparatory measures when a warning gives adequate lead time, and both are feasible with existing district machinery. Course III would mean beginning action only when it is too late to protect people. Therefore, courses I and II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Heavy rain has flooded the ground floor of a factory that stores electrical panels.

Courses of Action:
I. Switch off the supply to the affected area and move the panels and records to a dry place at the earliest.
II. Have the water pumped out and the affected panels inspected and certified before restarting production.
III. Restart production on the same day to protect the delivery schedule.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course II should be followed.
Courses II and III should be followed.
Courses I and II should be followed.
All three courses should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Courses I and II are necessary as an immediate measure and as a safe restoration step respectively. Course III risks an electrical accident or equipment failure and would put the delivery schedule at greater risk than a short stoppage. Therefore, courses I and II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A company has been asked to reduce its operating budget by fifteen per cent within a quarter.

Courses of Action:
I. Rank the current projects by business value and stop or defer the lowest-value work.
II. Renegotiate vendor contracts and review the largest recurring expenses on evidence.
III. Lay off a third of the workforce immediately without reviewing the work they do.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Courses I and II should be followed.
All three courses should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Courses I and II reduce spending in a planned way and can be achieved within the quarter. Course III is a drastic measure that would remove capacity the company may still need and was not based on any assessment of value. Therefore, courses I and II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
Frequent power fluctuations in an industrial unit are damaging electronic equipment on the shop floor.

Courses of Action:
I. Install proper surge protection and voltage stabilisation for the affected machines.
II. Escalate the fluctuation complaints to the electricity utility with recorded data for correction at the source.
III. Continue operations as they are and replace the equipment when it fails.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I should be followed.
Courses I and II should be followed.
Courses II and III should be followed.
All three courses should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Courses I and II protect the equipment and pursue the supply problem itself, which is the cause of the damage. Course III accepts repeated destruction of equipment as normal and would cost far more than either protective measure. Therefore, courses I and II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A software company's night-shift team has complained of fatigue and errors in their work.

Courses of Action:
I. Review the shift timing and rotation pattern against the workload and act on what the review shows.
II. Recruit additional staff so that the night shift can be shortened.
III. Ask the team to consume energy drinks and continue with the same schedule.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Courses I and III should be followed.
All three courses should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Courses I and II should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Courses I and II attack the fatigue through scheduling and staffing, which are factors the company controls. Course III treats the symptom with a temporary stimulant and leaves the exhausting schedule unchanged. Therefore, courses I and II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A college has to conduct an examination for two thousand students in a hall with a capacity of twelve hundred.

Courses of Action:
I. Hold the examination in two shifts with separate question papers.
II. Book additional halls in nearby schools and arrange seating and invigilation.
III. Conduct the examination in the same hall and allow students to share seats.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Courses II and III should be followed.
Courses I and II should be followed.
None of the courses should be followed.
Only course III should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Courses I and II both provide an orderly way to accommodate all the candidates, and either or both can be arranged with adequate notice. Course III would destroy the integrity of the examination and permit copying. Therefore, courses I and II should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A hospital's ambulance service is being used for non-urgent transport by a few staff members.

Courses of Action:
I. Ask the ambulance drivers to refuse any request that does not appear urgent to them.
II. Remove the ambulance from the smaller of the two facilities to reduce misuse.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I leaves the decision to individual drivers without any record or standard, which would not control misuse and could delay a genuine emergency. Course II reduces emergency capacity in response to a disciplinary issue. Therefore, neither course should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A state-run bus service is losing money on many routes while demand on a few routes is unmet.

Courses of Action:
I. Analyse route-wise ridership and cost, revise frequencies on weak routes and add services where demand exceeds capacity.
II. Withdraw all loss-making routes immediately and let private operators decide whether to run them.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.
Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I adjusts the network using the data that the operator already collects. Course II removes services from places that may have no alternative, which is a much larger decision than the information supports. Therefore, course I should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
Complaints about a municipal office are increasing because its staff do not give receipts for applications.

Courses of Action:
I. Make the receipt mandatory through a digital acknowledgement and make the pending-status visible to the applicant.
II. Ask the applicants to photograph the staff member they deal with.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I creates a verifiable record of every application, which is what the complaint is about. Course II does not create any institutional record and could create conflict at the counter. Therefore, only course I is justified.

questions.questionText:
A village panchayat's street-cleaning staff do not cover the whole village each week.

Courses of Action:
I. Prepare a ward-wise cleaning schedule, display it publicly and record completion with a supervisor's check.
II. Ask residents to clean the street in front of their own houses instead.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I makes the existing service accountable and complete. Course II shifts a paid service onto the residents without addressing the coverage gap. Therefore, course I is the better course of action.

questions.questionText:
A district's public distribution system data shows large differences between the stock issued and the quantity distributed.

Courses of Action:
I. Audit the stock registers of the dealers concerned, install electronic weighing and point-of-sale devices at the shops and act on the audit findings.
II. Increase the quantity allotted to the district to cover the difference.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I identifies where the stock is going and adds the controls that would prevent it. Course II supplies more stock to a system that is already losing it. Therefore, only course I should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A government hospital's pharmacy frequently runs out of essential medicines.

Courses of Action:
I. Use consumption data to set reorder levels, and track stock with a simple digital inventory that raises an alert at the threshold.
II. Ask patients to buy the medicines from outside and claim reimbursement later.
III. Allow the pharmacy to buy from local suppliers at short notice for items that have run out.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course III should be followed.
Courses I and III should be followed.
None of the courses should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I prevents stock-outs with forecasting and control. Course II transfers the cost to patients and does not improve availability. Course III is appropriate as a fallback because it keeps essential medicines available while the reorder levels are being corrected. Therefore, courses I and III should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A city's public bicycle scheme has very few users, and the cycles are lying idle.

Courses of Action:
I. Survey why people are not using it and adjust the docking locations, timings and pricing accordingly.
II. Remove all the cycles because the scheme has failed.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both courses should be implemented.
Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I finds the reason for non-use and adapts the service. Course II terminates a public investment without learning what would have made it work. Therefore, course I should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
A local body's complaint helpline is answered only during office hours, and most complaints are made in the evening.

Courses of Action:
I. Extend the helpline to the evening hours when the calls arrive and route the calls to the concerned department the next morning.
II. Ask callers to record their complaints and call back during office hours.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I matches the service hours to when the demand actually occurs. Course II repeats the same mismatch that causes the problem. Therefore, only course I is justified.

questions.questionText:
A university's results portal crashes on the day results are declared.

Courses of Action:
I. Plan for the expected load, add capacity before the declaration and publish the results in batches.
II. Declare the results only at the counter so that the portal is not used.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I prepares for a demand that is entirely predictable. Course II removes the convenient channel and would create large queues on campus. Therefore, course I is the better course of action.

questions.questionText:
A town's weekly market creates traffic problems on the main road every week.

Courses of Action:
I. Relocate the market to a designated ground or shift the road's traffic management for the market day.
II. Ban the market and ask traders to find their own premises.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I addresses the conflict between the market and the road while keeping the market. Course II destroys a source of livelihood because of a traffic problem that can be planned for. Therefore, only course I should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A municipality's garbage vehicles are frequently out of service and repairs take weeks.

Courses of Action:
I. Schedule preventive maintenance for the fleet, keep essential spares in stock and hire vehicles temporarily when the fleet is short.
II. Ask the residents to segregate and compost their own waste so that less collection is needed.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.
Neither course should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I keeps the collection service running. Course II reduces the waste to be collected, but the fleet problem would still leave the remaining waste uncollected. Therefore, course I should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
Several students at a government school cannot afford the prescribed uniforms and are staying away for that reason.

Courses of Action:
I. Provide uniforms free of cost to the identified students through the existing welfare scheme and record their attendance separately.
II. Relax the uniform rule and allow the affected students to attend in any dress.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I addresses the barrier that keeps the students away and uses an existing scheme. Course II adjusts the school's rule but does not remove the reason the students are absent. Therefore, only course I is justified.

questions.questionText:
A village's only health centre has no doctor on two days of the week.

Courses of Action:
I. Fix a roster with a visiting doctor on those days and inform the village of the schedule in advance.
II. Ask patients to travel to the district hospital on those days.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I maintains the service by arranging cover on the days it is missing. Course II sends patients much further at their own cost, which is hardest on those who need the centre most. Therefore, course I is the better course of action.

questions.questionText:
A public examination centre's CCTV footage was found to be unavailable for one of the sessions.

Courses of Action:
I. Secure the recorded footage of the other sessions, report the gap to the examination authority and review the functioning of the system before the next session.
II. Assume that nothing irregular happened because no complaint was received.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I preserves the available evidence and reports an oversight that affects the credibility of the examination. Course II accepts the absence of footage as proof that nothing occurred. Therefore, only course I should be followed.

questions.questionText:
An industrial estate's common effluent treatment plant is running above its capacity.

Courses of Action:
I. Measure the load from each unit, require in-house pre-treatment from the largest contributors and plan an expansion of the plant.
II. Release the partially treated effluent at night when it is less visible.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I reduces the load and improves the treatment capacity in an orderly way. Course II releases untreated pollution into the environment at a time when it is less likely to be noticed. Therefore, course I should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
A state's road transport corporation has many buses off the road because of a shortage of spare parts.

Courses of Action:
I. Simplify the procurement of standard spares, hold a minimum inventory and carry out repairs in batches so that services are not cut.
II. Reduce the number of daily services until the parts arrive.
III. Convert half of the older buses to run on a different fuel.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Courses I and II should be followed.
All three courses should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I repairs more buses and keeps services running. Course II reduces the service that passengers depend on while the underlying procurement problem continues. Course III addresses fuel rather than spare parts, and the conversion would consume the money that is needed for repairs. Therefore, only course I should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A district's schools have reported a shortage of teachers in mathematics and science.

Courses of Action:
I. Post additional teachers to the vacancies and, in the interim, arrange shared or visiting teachers across nearby schools.
II. Combine two classes of different standards and let one teacher handle both.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I closes the shortage and manages the interim period sensibly. Course II halves the attention available to two groups of students and does not add a teacher. Therefore, only course I is justified.

questions.questionText:
Many first-generation learners in a district discontinue their studies after school.

Courses of Action:
I. Provide information about higher-study options, arrange mentoring and link the students to the existing scholarship schemes.
II. Leave the decision to the families, since higher study is a personal choice.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I overcomes the information and support gap that makes such students leave education early. Course II leaves a known barrier unattended when the district already has the means to address it. Therefore, course I is the better course of action.

questions.questionText:
A city's lakes are being informally used for washing vehicles and dumping construction debris.

Courses of Action:
