I. Mark and enforce the protected zones of the lake, clean the debris and run an awareness programme with the resident associations.
II. Fence the lakes completely so that no citizen can approach them.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I stops the misuse and restores the water body while keeping it accessible. Course II prevents legitimate public use instead of preventing the specific misuse. Therefore, only course I should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A factory employs contract workers whose safety training records are incomplete.

Courses of Action:
I. Complete the training records, train the workers who have not been covered and make the record a condition for deployment.
II. Deploy only the workers whose records are available, whatever the production requirement.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both courses should be implemented.
Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I closes the gap in training and in documentation. Course II solves the paperwork by leaving a part of the workforce untrained and idle. Therefore, course I should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
A charitable trust running a shelter is running out of space during the monsoon.

Courses of Action:
I. Open an additional temporary shelter with basic facilities and coordinate with the local authority for a longer-term building.
II. Restrict entry to the shelter to a fixed number of people.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I increases capacity for the period when need is highest. Course II turns away people in the exact season when the shelter is most needed. Therefore, only course I is justified.

questions.questionText:
A district's emergency helpline is receiving calls that are not emergencies, and real calls are sometimes missed.

Courses of Action:
I. Separate the non-emergency calls into a different queue with staff guidance to callers, and record why calls are misdirected.
II. Block the numbers of callers who make non-emergency calls.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I reduces the load on the emergency queue without cutting anyone off. Course II risks blocking a number that may later have a genuine emergency. Therefore, course I is the better course of action.

questions.questionText:
A slum settlement has one public tap for more than two hundred families.

Courses of Action:
I. Extend the piped network with additional stand-posts and fix the supply hours so that the queue is distributed.
II. Fix a time slot for each family to collect water.
III. Install a spring-loaded tap and a small storage tank so that water is not wasted at the stand-post.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Courses I and III should be followed.
All three courses should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.
Courses I and II should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I increases the availability of the service. Course II allocates a shortage rather than reducing it. Course III is appropriate because it reduces wastage at the collection point and improves availability without adding a source. Therefore, courses I and III should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A state welfare scheme requires beneficiaries to submit a life certificate in person every year, and many elderly beneficiaries find this difficult.

Courses of Action:
I. Accept the certificate through a bank branch, a digital route or a visit by a welfare official, and publicise the options.
II. Extend the validity of the certificate to five years without changing the process.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I removes the burden from those who cannot travel easily. Course II makes the inconvenience rarer but keeps it, and it weakens verification of the beneficiary's status. Therefore, only course I should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A municipality's street-cleaning contracts are awarded afresh every year to the lowest bidder, and service quality falls in the first months.

Courses of Action:
I. Include service history and minimum staffing in the evaluation, and publish a performance score that influences the next award.
II. Award a five-year contract to the same contractor without any performance condition.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both courses should be implemented.
Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I links the award to performance so that quality is considered along with price. Course II removes competition while leaving the quality problem unmanaged. Therefore, course I should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
An industrial park's internal roads are used as a shortcut by heavy trucks from outside.

Courses of Action:
I. Install access control at the entrances, provide adequate signage and coordinate with the local traffic authority for enforcement.
II. Dig up the internal roads so that they become unusable for trucks.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.
Both courses are justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I regulates access and keeps the roads usable for the estates' own traffic. Course II damages the infrastructure to protect it, which harms the firms that use it. Therefore, only course I is justified.

questions.questionText:
A district has surplus food grain in storage while some households in the same district report food insecurity.

Courses of Action:
I. Verify the coverage of the existing distribution scheme and extend it or arrange community kitchens where the gap is confirmed.
II. Sell the surplus in the open market and use the proceeds for other schemes.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I connects the available supply with the reported need. Course II converts a resource that could address a present need into revenue for unrelated purposes. Therefore, course I is the better course of action.

questions.questionText:
A state's public buses do not have a working complaint mechanism for passengers.

Courses of Action:
I. Place a helpline number and a scannable complaint code in every bus and publish the resolution times for common complaints.
II. Ask passengers to write in a register maintained at the depot.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Only course II should be followed.
Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I gives passengers a channel that is available where the problem occurs. Course II requires travel to a depot, which most passengers will not do. Therefore, only course I should be followed.

questions.questionText:
A college's anti-ragging committee has not met even once in the academic year.

Courses of Action:
I. Mandate and record regular meetings, publish the committee members and the reporting route, and act on complaints within defined timelines.
II. Disband the committee since there have been no reported incidents.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.
Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I makes the safeguard visible and active, which is how complaints reach the committee. Course II removes the mechanism whose absence is the reason incidents go unreported. Therefore, course I should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
A city has installed public bicycle docks but the payment kiosks do not accept cards.

Courses of Action:
I. Enable multiple payment modes including the national payment interface and the transport card.
II. Remove the kiosks and collect charges in cash.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I removes a practical barrier that keeps users away. Course II returns to a slower, cash-based process that would reduce usage further. Therefore, only course I is justified.

questions.questionText:
A hospital's biomedical waste is not being segregated at the point of generation.

Courses of Action:
I. Train the staff and provide colour-coded bins at each point of generation, with a daily audit of the segregation.
II. Ask the waste contractor to segregate the waste at the disposal site.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.
Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I puts segregation where it belongs and can be verified. Course II moves the task to the disposal site, where mixed waste is already a hazard and cannot be safely separated. Therefore, course I is the better course of action.

questions.questionText:
A state's teachers are spending a large part of the school day on non-teaching administrative work.

Courses of Action:
I. Map the administrative tasks, move the data-entry work to a central clerical pool and simplify the reporting formats.
II. Ask the teachers to complete the administrative work after school hours.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both courses I and II should be followed.
Neither course should be followed.
Only course I should be followed.
Only course II should be followed.

questions.explanationText: Course I removes the non-teaching burden from teaching hours. Course II extends the working day of the teachers without reducing the workload that causes the problem. Therefore, only course I should be followed.

questions.questionText:
An office's employees are not reporting workplace injuries because they fear it will affect their appraisal.

Courses of Action:
I. Separate the safety reporting from the appraisal process, make reporting confidential and review the workplace risks that cause the injuries.
II. Ask employees to report injuries only if they require hospital treatment.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Course II should be implemented.
Both courses should be implemented.
Neither course should be implemented.
Course I should be implemented.

questions.explanationText: Course I removes the reason for under-reporting and addresses the hazards themselves. Course II leaves a threshold that would keep the less serious injuries out of the record. Therefore, course I should be implemented.

questions.questionText:
A municipal corporation must repair a water pipeline that serves a densely populated ward, and the work will need digging along a main road.

Courses of Action:
I. Carry out the repair in phases and schedule the digging at night so that traffic is disturbed only outside the peak hours.
II. Inform the residents in advance about the days on which the supply will be interrupted and arrange tanker supply for those days.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both courses are justified.
Neither course is justified.
Only course I is justified.
Only course II is justified.

questions.explanationText: Course I keeps the road usable during the hours when traffic is heaviest, which is the main disruption the work would cause. Course II protects the households that will lose their supply during the repair. Both are practical and together they cover the two effects of the work. Therefore, both courses are justified.

questions.questionText:
A college's sports team has lost most of its matches this season.

Courses of Action:
I. Cancel the remaining matches of the season so that the team's record is not spoiled further.
II. Criticise the players publicly for the results without reviewing the coaching or the practice facilities.

Which of the following courses of action should be followed?

options.text: Both are reasonable courses of action.
Neither is a reasonable course of action.
Course I is the better course of action.
Course II is the better course of action.

questions.explanationText: Course I withdraws the team from competition instead of improving it and denies the players the experience they need. Course II places the blame on the players while leaving the coaching and facilities unexamined. Neither course addresses the team's performance. Therefore, neither is a reasonable course of action.
